playbooks.title: Engine cranks but does not start
playbooks.summary: Confirm the basics first: adequate cranking voltage, a valid RPM signal, security authorization, fuel pressure, and spark. Scan data taken while cranking quickly separates sensor, immobilizer, and module power faults from fuel delivery and mechanical causes. Measure fuel pressure and spark directly before condemning a pump or sensor, and verify mechanical timing only after the non-invasive checks point that way.
clarifyingQuestions: Did the engine stall while driving and then refuse to restart, or fail to start after sitting?
Does the engine crank at normal speed, or does it crank slowly?
Does the security or immobilizer indicator flash or stay on with the key on?
Does the tachometer move while cranking?
Any recent work, low-fuel event, collision, or fill-up just before the problem started?
Does it fail to start only hot, only cold, or all the time?

causes.title: Failed fuel pump
causes.description: A pump that no longer runs or cannot build pressure leaves the injectors without fuel even though the engine cranks normally.

modifiers.reason: Sudden loss of fuel delivery often appears as a stall followed by a no-start
Worn pumps commonly fail when hot
Pump wear increases with age

causes.title: Fuel pump power, ground, or control circuit fault
causes.description: An open fuse, failed relay or pump driver module, tripped inertia switch (where equipped), or high-resistance wiring prevents the pump from receiving adequate power.

modifiers.reason: Fuel pump primary/secondary circuit code present
Fuel pump control circuit code present
An impact fuel cutoff may have tripped on equipped vehicles

causes.title: Insufficient fuel pressure
causes.description: A weak pump, restricted filter or pickup, faulty regulator, or pressure leak-down leaves some pressure but not enough to start, often with long cranking.

modifiers.reason: Fuel rail/system pressure too low code present
Loss of residual pressure causes long cranking

causes.title: Crankshaft position sensor or circuit fault
causes.description: Without a crankshaft signal the engine controller sees no RPM and typically commands neither spark nor injection.

modifiers.reason: Crankshaft position sensor code present
No tachometer movement while cranking suggests a missing RPM signal
Crank sensors commonly fail when heat-soaked

causes.title: Camshaft position sensor or circuit fault
causes.description: Some engine management systems will not synchronize injection or spark without a valid camshaft signal, causing a no-start or very long crank.

modifiers.reason: Camshaft position sensor code present

causes.title: Immobilizer or anti-theft system inhibiting start
causes.description: When the key or fob is not authenticated, the security system disables fuel injection, ignition, or both while still allowing the engine to crank on many vehicles.

modifiers.reason: Immobilizer key or programming code present

modifiers.match: security|theft|immobiliz|key light|flashing key|new key|spare key|key fob
modifiers.reason: Security indicator or key-related complaint

causes.title: Ignition coil power or control circuit fault
causes.description: Loss of the shared coil power feed (fuse, relay, or wiring) or of the coil control circuits removes spark on all cylinders.

modifiers.reason: No spark reported
Ignition coil circuit codes present

causes.title: Timing belt or chain jumped or broken
causes.description: Incorrect or lost valve timing reduces cylinder compression and crank/cam correlation, so the engine cranks, often with an unusual even or fast sound, but cannot start.

modifiers.reason: Crankshaft/camshaft correlation code present

modifiers.match: timing belt|timing chain|cranks fast|cranks faster|sounds different|rattle|backfire
modifiers.reason: Abnormal cranking sound or timing component history
Belt and chain wear increase with mileage

causes.title: Module power or ground circuit fault
causes.description: A failed main relay, open fuse, or poor ground at the engine controller leaves it unpowered or unstable, so it cannot command fuel or spark and may not communicate.

modifiers.reason: Other modules report lost communication with the ECM/PCM
Scan tool cannot communicate with the engine controller

causes.title: Low system voltage
causes.description: A weak battery or high-resistance cable lets voltage sag during cranking, so modules reset or the ignition and fuel systems cannot operate even though the starter turns the engine.

modifiers.reason: Slow cranking or weak battery complaint
System voltage code present

tests.title: Check battery voltage and cranking speed during cranking
tests.purpose: Rule out low system voltage before interpreting any other no-start data.
procedure: Measure open-circuit battery voltage with all loads off and note state of charge.
Connect the meter leads directly to the battery posts (not the cable clamps).
Crank the engine for no longer than the OEM cranking limit while recording minimum voltage and listening to cranking speed.
If voltage is low, charge the battery and repeat before continuing the diagnosis.
tools: Digital multimeter or scan tool voltage PID
tests.expected: Battery voltage remains above the OEM minimum while cranking and cranking speed sounds normal (general guideline: a healthy 12 V system typically stays above roughly 9.6 V at about 70 °F / 21 °C — verify against OEM specification).
tests.specNote: OEM minimum cranking voltage and maximum cranking duration.

outcomes.label: Cranking voltage and speed normal
outcomes.interpretation: System voltage is adequate; continue with scan data, fuel, and spark checks.

outcomes.label: Voltage drops below the minimum or cranking is slow
outcomes.interpretation: Charge and test the battery and check cable voltage drop before continuing; repeated cranking attempts can also deplete a good battery.

outcomes.label: Battery was depleted by repeated cranking attempts
outcomes.interpretation: Charge the battery fully and repeat the test before drawing conclusions.

tests.title: Scan for DTCs and review RPM, security, and communication while cranking
tests.purpose: Separate missing RPM signal, immobilizer inhibit, and engine controller power faults from fuel and mechanical causes.
procedure: Connect a scan tool, key on, and confirm communication with the engine controller.
Record DTCs and freeze frame data from all modules, including the body and security modules.
Observe the security indicator and any immobilizer status data available for the vehicle.
Display engine RPM and crank the engine within the OEM cranking limit.
Record whether RPM is reported while cranking and whether communication remains stable.
tests.expected: The engine controller communicates, no security fault is present, and RPM is reported while cranking.

outcomes.label: Communicates, RPM reported, no security fault
outcomes.interpretation: Crank signal, security, and controller power are likely fine; focus on fuel delivery, spark, and mechanical timing.

outcomes.label: RPM reads zero while cranking
outcomes.interpretation: The controller is not seeing a crankshaft signal; test the crankshaft position sensor circuit and signal.

outcomes.label: Security indicator or immobilizer data shows the key is not authorized
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the immobilizer system per OEM procedure before testing fuel or spark.

outcomes.label: No communication with the engine controller
outcomes.interpretation: Check engine controller power, ground, and main relay circuits, and the data link connection.

outcomes.label: Scan tool could not access the needed data
outcomes.interpretation: Use a scope on the sensor signals or a different scan tool; probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Check key recognition with a known-good programmed spare key
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out an immobilizer or key authentication fault.
procedure: Observe the security indicator behavior with the original key and note any immobilizer DTCs or status data.
Try a known-good, already-programmed spare key or fob, holding it in the OEM backup location if the fob battery may be weak.
Attempt a start and record whether the security indicator and status data change.
Do not attempt key programming or module replacement without the OEM security access procedure.
tools: Scan tool with body/security module access
tests.expected: The key is recognized (security indicator behaves normally and no immobilizer fault is reported).
tests.specNote: OEM immobilizer indicator behavior and key programming procedures.

outcomes.label: Key recognized, no security inhibit
outcomes.interpretation: The immobilizer is unlikely to be the cause; continue with fuel and spark checks.

outcomes.label: Engine starts with the spare key
outcomes.interpretation: The original key or fob transponder is likely at fault; follow OEM key diagnosis and programming procedures.

outcomes.label: Neither key is recognized
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the immobilizer antenna, module communication, and power/ground per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: No programmed spare key available
outcomes.interpretation: Rely on security status data and DTCs; probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Listen for fuel pump operation at key-on or when commanded
tests.purpose: Determine whether the fuel pump is being powered and running.
procedure: With the key off, have an assistant turn the key on (engine off) while you listen at the fuel tank or filler neck.
If the vehicle supports it, command the fuel pump on with the scan tool output control.
Listen for the pump hum during the prime period; repeat once to confirm.
tools: Scan tool with output controls (if supported)
tests.expected: The pump runs audibly during the prime period or when commanded.

outcomes.label: Pump runs
outcomes.interpretation: The pump is powered; verify it produces pressure with a gauge.

outcomes.label: Pump does not run
outcomes.interpretation: Check fuses, relay, and pump power and ground at the pump connector before condemning the pump.

outcomes.label: Pump could not be heard
outcomes.interpretation: Background noise or tank design prevents a conclusion; measure fuel pressure instead.

tests.title: Check for spark with an adjustable spark tester
tests.purpose: Determine whether the ignition system is producing adequate spark while cranking.
procedure: Disable fuel delivery per OEM procedure so raw fuel is not pumped into the cylinders during testing.
Connect an adjustable spark tester to a coil output or plug lead and ground it to a clean engine ground; never hold the tester or leads while cranking.
Set the gap per the tester manufacturer's instructions for the ignition system type.
Crank the engine and observe the spark; repeat on at least two other cylinders.
Restore fuel delivery when testing is complete.
tests.expected: A strong, consistent spark jumps the tester gap on each cylinder tested.

outcomes.label: Strong spark on all tested cylinders
outcomes.interpretation: Ignition is working; focus on fuel delivery and mechanical timing.

outcomes.label: No spark on any tested cylinder
outcomes.interpretation: A common fault is likely: RPM signal, coil power feed, or controller power. Check the crank signal and coil supply before any coil.

outcomes.label: Weak or intermittent spark
outcomes.interpretation: Check system voltage during cranking, the coil supply voltage drop, and the crank signal quality.

outcomes.label: Coil outputs could not be accessed safely
outcomes.interpretation: Use scan data or a scope on coil control circuits instead; probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Measure fuel pressure at key-on and while cranking
tests.purpose: Verify the fuel system delivers and holds the specified pressure.
procedure: Wear eye protection, keep ignition sources away, and have a fire extinguisher nearby.

Connect a fuel pressure gauge to the service port per OEM procedure; on returnless or direct-injection systems use the OEM-approved method, such as a low-side pressure PID. Never open the high-pressure side of a direct-injection system.
Cycle the key on and record prime pressure, then crank and record pressure while cranking.
Turn the key off and record pressure leak-down over the OEM-specified time.
Relieve pressure per OEM procedure before disconnecting the gauge and wrap the fitting with a shop towel.
tools: Scan tool (for pressure PID on returnless/DI systems)
tests.expected: Pressure reaches and holds the OEM-specified value at key-on and while cranking, and leak-down stays within specification.
tests.specNote: OEM fuel pressure and leak-down specifications for the vehicle.

outcomes.label: Pressure within specification and holds
outcomes.interpretation: Fuel delivery is adequate; focus on spark, injector command, and mechanical causes.

outcomes.label: No fuel pressure
outcomes.interpretation: Test pump power and ground at the pump connector under load before replacing the pump.

outcomes.label: Low pressure or rapid leak-down
outcomes.interpretation: Check pump supply voltage drop, filter or pickup restriction, regulator, and check-valve or injector leak-down per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: No test port or pressure PID available
outcomes.interpretation: Use the OEM-approved alternative method; probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Check for injector command while cranking
tests.purpose: Determine whether the engine controller is commanding the injectors.
procedure: On port fuel injection, connect a noid light of the correct type to an injector connector; on direct injection do not use a noid light — injector drive voltage is elevated, so use scan data or a scope with OEM-approved leads.
Crank the engine and observe the noid light or waveform.
Check at least two injectors, including one on each bank where applicable.
Reconnect all injectors and clear any DTCs set by the test.
tests.expected: Injector pulses are present on each tested injector while cranking.

outcomes.label: Injector pulse present
outcomes.interpretation: The controller is commanding fuel; confirm pressure, spark, and mechanical condition.

outcomes.label: No injector pulse
outcomes.interpretation: Look for a common cause: RPM or cam signal, immobilizer inhibit, controller power, or a shared injector/coil supply fuse.

outcomes.label: Injectors not accessible
outcomes.interpretation: Use scan data for injector pulse width while cranking; probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Relative compression test using cranking current
tests.purpose: Detect uniformly low compression from jumped or broken timing without disassembly.
procedure: Disable fuel and ignition per OEM procedure so the engine cannot start.
Clamp a high-amperage current probe around the battery or starter cable and connect it to a lab scope.
Crank the engine for a few seconds and capture the current waveform.
Compare the height and spacing of the compression peaks and listen for an unusually fast or even cranking sound.
Restore fuel and ignition when finished.
tests.expected: Compression peaks are pronounced and even, and cranking sounds normal.

outcomes.label: Even, pronounced compression peaks
outcomes.interpretation: Mechanical timing loss is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Flat or uniformly low peaks with fast cranking
outcomes.interpretation: Compression is low across cylinders; verify crank/cam correlation and mechanical timing.

tests.title: Scope crankshaft and camshaft signals while cranking
tests.purpose: Confirm each position signal is present and that crank/cam correlation is correct.
procedure: Identify the crank and cam sensor signal circuits from the OEM wiring diagram.
Backprobe the signal wires with scope leads, avoiding pierced insulation, and connect grounds to a clean engine ground.
Disable fuel per OEM procedure, crank the engine, and capture both signals at the same time.
Compare the pattern and the crank-to-cam relationship to a known-good reference or OEM pattern.
tests.expected: Both signals are present with clean patterns and correct crank-to-cam alignment per the reference.
tests.specNote: OEM crank/cam signal pattern or a verified known-good waveform for the engine.

outcomes.label: Both signals present and correctly aligned
outcomes.interpretation: Position sensing and timing are correct; look elsewhere.

outcomes.label: Crank signal missing or distorted
outcomes.interpretation: Check the sensor supply and ground, wiring, air gap, and reluctor before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: Cam signal missing or distorted
outcomes.interpretation: Check the cam sensor supply, ground, and wiring before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: Signals present but crank/cam alignment is incorrect
outcomes.interpretation: Mechanical timing has likely shifted; verify timing marks before other repairs.

outcomes.label: No reference waveform available for comparison
outcomes.interpretation: Signal presence can still be judged; correlation needs a reference. Probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Voltage drop test of the fuel pump power and ground circuits under load
tests.purpose: Distinguish a failed pump from a supply, relay, or ground fault.
procedure: Locate the pump connector and circuits using the OEM wiring diagram.
Backprobe the pump supply and ground terminals without disconnecting the pump so the circuit stays loaded.
Command the pump on with the scan tool or during key-on prime.
Measure supply voltage at the pump, then voltage drop from battery positive to the pump supply terminal and from the pump ground terminal to battery negative.
Do not jumper battery power directly to the pump without fused protection.
tests.expected: Supply voltage is present and voltage drop on each side is within OEM specification (general guideline: a few tenths of a volt per side on a motor circuit — verify against OEM specification).
tests.specNote: OEM fuel pump circuit voltage and voltage drop specifications.

outcomes.label: Good supply and ground under load at the pump
outcomes.interpretation: The circuit is delivering power; if the pump still does not run or build pressure, the pump assembly is implicated.

outcomes.label: No supply voltage at the pump when commanded
outcomes.interpretation: Trace the fuse, relay or driver module, inertia switch, and control command back from the pump.

outcomes.label: Excessive voltage drop on the supply or ground side
outcomes.interpretation: Locate the high-resistance point by measuring drop across each connector, relay, and ground in the circuit.

tests.title: Check engine controller power feeds and grounds under load
tests.purpose: Confirm the engine controller has good power, ignition feed, and grounds.
procedure: Identify the controller battery, ignition, main relay, and ground circuits from the OEM wiring diagram.
Backprobe the circuits at the controller connector with the connector installed.
With the key on (and while cranking if possible), measure supply voltages and the voltage drop across each ground to battery negative.
Use a low-current test light only where the OEM permits, and never on sensor reference or signal circuits.
tests.expected: All supplies are present and ground voltage drops are within OEM specification.
tests.specNote: OEM controller power and ground circuit identification and limits.

outcomes.label: All power feeds and grounds good
outcomes.interpretation: Controller power supply is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Missing feed or excessive ground drop
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the open or high-resistance circuit and retest before considering controller replacement.

tests.title: Verify mechanical valve timing
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out a jumped or broken timing belt or chain.
procedure: Disconnect the battery negative cable and follow the OEM procedure to access the timing marks or inspection points.
Rotate the engine by hand only in the normal direction of rotation to the OEM reference position.
Compare camshaft and crankshaft marks to the OEM alignment and inspect the belt or chain, guides, and tensioner.
On interference engines, do not crank the engine further if the belt or chain is broken.
tools: OEM timing procedure and alignment tools
tests.expected: Timing marks align per OEM specification and the belt or chain is intact.
tests.specNote: OEM timing mark locations and alignment procedure.

outcomes.label: Timing marks aligned, drive intact
outcomes.interpretation: Mechanical timing is correct.

outcomes.label: Marks misaligned or belt/chain broken
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the timing drive; on interference engines check for valve damage before returning the vehicle.

verification: Record and then clear DTCs in all modules.
Start the engine several times cold and again after a heat soak.
Confirm scan data shows RPM while cranking, normal security status, and fuel pressure within OEM specification.
Road test and recheck all modules for pending DTCs.

playbooks.title: Engine does not crank
playbooks.summary: Classify the complaint by what happens at the start attempt (nothing, a single click, or rapid clicking) and prove battery condition before touching the starter. Voltage drop testing of the battery cables and the solenoid control circuit under load finds high-resistance connections that an ohmmeter misses. Condemn the starter only after battery, cables, grounds, start interlocks, security authorization, and control voltage are verified.
clarifyingQuestions: At the start attempt, do you hear nothing, a single click, rapid clicking, or the starter spinning?
Do the dash lights and headlights stay bright, dim, or go out during the start attempt?
Does it crank if the shifter is moved to Neutral, or with the clutch or brake pedal pressed firmly?
Was the battery or a cable recently replaced, or has the vehicle needed jump-starts?
Is the security or key indicator flashing, or is a 'key not detected' message displayed?

causes.title: Weak or failed battery
causes.description: A discharged or failed battery cannot supply cranking current; voltage collapses under load and the solenoid chatters or nothing happens.

modifiers.reason: Rapid clicking, dimming lights, or jump-start history point to low battery capacity
Cold reduces available battery capacity
System voltage code present

causes.title: Loose or corroded battery terminal or cable
causes.description: High resistance at a battery terminal or inside a cable limits starter current even with a good battery; it often appears as a click with no crank or an intermittent no-crank.

modifiers.reason: Terminal condition or intermittent behavior reported
Solenoid engages but current is limited

causes.title: Poor ground connection
causes.description: A corroded, loose, or missing engine-to-battery or engine-to-body ground strap adds resistance to the starter return path.

modifiers.match: ground strap|engine work|transmission work|clutch replaced|transmission replaced
modifiers.reason: Recent work can leave a ground strap disconnected or loose

causes.title: Failed starter motor or solenoid
causes.description: Worn brushes, burnt solenoid contacts, an open or shorted armature, or a failed drive prevents the starter from turning the engine despite good power and control voltage.

modifiers.reason: Single click, whir, or grind points to the starter or its drive
Heat-soaked starters often fail to engage
Starter wear increases with age

causes.title: Starter control circuit fault
causes.description: An open fuse, failed starter relay, worn ignition switch or start button input, or damaged wiring to the solenoid control terminal prevents the solenoid from being energized.

modifiers.reason: Starter request or starter relay circuit code present
No solenoid click suggests no control voltage

causes.title: Start interlock input fault (range, clutch, or brake switch)
causes.description: A misadjusted or failed transmission range switch, clutch pedal switch, or brake pedal switch (push-button start) prevents the start request from being enabled.

modifiers.reason: Complaint involves the shifter, clutch, brake pedal, or push-button start
Transmission range sensor circuit code present
Clutch pedal switch circuit code present
Brake switch code present (push-button start systems)

causes.title: Immobilizer or anti-theft system inhibiting start
causes.description: On many vehicles an unauthenticated key or fob blocks the start request or starter relay, so nothing happens at the start attempt.

modifiers.reason: Immobilizer key or programming code present

modifiers.match: security|theft|immobiliz|key light|flashing key|key not detected|key fob
modifiers.reason: Security indicator or key detection complaint

causes.title: Engine mechanically seized or hydrolocked
causes.description: Internal damage or liquid in a cylinder stops the crankshaft from turning; the solenoid clicks and the starter draws very high current without rotation.

modifiers.match: seized|locked up|water|flood|hydro|oil light|ran out of oil|loud knock
modifiers.reason: Water ingestion, oil starvation, or internal noise history

tests.title: Observe the start attempt: sounds and dash lights
tests.purpose: Classify the failure as no response, single click, rapid clicking, or starter spin to focus the diagnosis.
procedure: Turn on the headlights or watch the dash lights so voltage behavior is visible.
Make a start attempt while an assistant listens near the starter.
Note whether there is no sound, a single solid click, rapid clicking, or the starter spinning without turning the engine.
Note whether the lights stay bright, dim heavily, or go out.
tests.expected: The engine cranks normally with only a slight dimming of the lights.

outcomes.label: Nothing happens; lights stay bright
outcomes.interpretation: The solenoid is probably not being energized; check interlocks, security status, and control voltage.

outcomes.label: Single click with no crank; lights stay mostly bright
outcomes.interpretation: The solenoid engages but the motor does not turn; check cable voltage drop, starter, and engine rotation.

outcomes.label: Rapid clicking or lights dim heavily or go out
outcomes.interpretation: Voltage collapses under load; test the battery and the cable connections first.

outcomes.label: Starter spins or whirs without turning the engine
outcomes.interpretation: The starter drive is not engaging; inspect the starter drive and flywheel ring gear.

outcomes.label: Engine cranked normally; complaint not reproduced
outcomes.interpretation: Intermittent fault; leave a meter connected and repeat start attempts hot and cold. Probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Battery state of charge and load or conductance test
tests.purpose: Determine whether the battery can deliver cranking current.
procedure: Wear eye protection, avoid sparks near the battery, and do not test or charge a frozen battery.
Measure open-circuit voltage after removing surface charge, with all loads off.
If state of charge is low, charge the battery per the charger and battery manufacturer instructions for its type (flooded, EFB, or AGM).
Perform a conductance test or a load test per the tester and battery manufacturer instructions, using the rated CCA from the battery label.
Record results and compare to the tester's pass/fail criteria.
tools: Conductance tester or carbon-pile load tester
tests.expected: The battery is fully charged and passes the load or conductance test (general guideline: about 12.6 V open-circuit indicates a fully charged flooded 12 V battery at room temperature — verify against the battery manufacturer specification).
tests.specNote: Battery rated CCA and the manufacturer's test criteria for its type.

outcomes.label: Fully charged and passes the test
outcomes.interpretation: The battery is capable; move on to cables, grounds, and the starter circuit.

outcomes.label: Low state of charge that will not recover, or fails the load/conductance test
outcomes.interpretation: Replace or recharge the battery as indicated and find out why it was discharged (charging system or parasitic draw) before returning the vehicle.

outcomes.label: Battery too deeply discharged to test
outcomes.interpretation: Charge fully and retest; a surface charge can mask a failed battery.

tests.title: Check start interlocks: shifter position, clutch, and brake inputs
tests.purpose: Determine whether a range, clutch, or brake switch input is blocking the start request.
procedure: Apply the parking brake and chock the wheels; the engine may crank unexpectedly during this check.
Attempt a start in Park, then in Neutral, and while moving the shifter slightly within the position.
On manual transmissions, press the clutch fully; on push-button start vehicles, press the brake pedal firmly.
With a scan tool, check the transmission range, clutch switch, and brake switch status data against the actual positions.
tests.expected: The vehicle cranks in Park and Neutral, and switch status data match the actual positions.

outcomes.label: Cranks only in another position or with the shifter moved
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect and adjust or test the range or clutch switch per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Switch status data do not match actual position
outcomes.interpretation: Test the switch and its circuit before replacing it.

outcomes.label: No change; switch status data correct
outcomes.interpretation: Start interlocks are unlikely to be the cause.

tests.title: Check immobilizer and key detection status
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the security system is blocking the start request.
procedure: Observe the security indicator and any key-detection messages at the start attempt.
With a scan tool, read DTCs and security or key status data in the body, security, and engine modules.
Try a known-good programmed spare key or fob, using the OEM backup location if the fob battery may be weak.
tools: Scan tool with body/security module access
tests.expected: The key is detected and authorized; no security DTCs are present.

outcomes.label: Key detected and authorized
outcomes.interpretation: The security system is not blocking the start.

outcomes.label: Key not detected or not authorized, or security DTCs present
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the immobilizer per OEM procedure; key programming requires OEM security access.

tests.title: Voltage drop test of the battery positive and ground cables during a start attempt
tests.purpose: Locate high resistance in the main cranking circuit under actual load.
procedure: Confirm the battery is charged and passes testing.
Connect the meter from the battery positive post (not the clamp) to the starter B+ terminal and make a start attempt; record the reading.
Connect the meter from the battery negative post to the starter housing or engine block and make a start attempt; record the reading.
If a reading is high, move the lead point by point (clamp, cable end, junction, ground strap) to isolate the high-resistance connection.
Keep hands, leads, and clothing clear of belts and the fan.
tests.expected: Voltage drop on each side of the circuit is within OEM specification (general guideline: roughly 0.5 V or less on the positive side and about 0.3 V or less on the ground side during cranking — verify against OEM specification).
tests.specNote: OEM starter circuit voltage drop limits.

outcomes.label: Both sides within specification
outcomes.interpretation: Main cables and grounds are good; check solenoid control voltage and the starter.

outcomes.label: Excessive drop on the positive side
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or repair the positive terminal, cable, or junction and retest.

outcomes.label: Excessive drop on the ground side
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or repair the negative terminal, ground cable, or engine ground strap and retest.

tests.title: Check starter relay command, fuse, and relay output
tests.purpose: Determine whether the start request reaches the starter relay and whether the relay switches.
procedure: Check the starter circuit fuses with a meter or test light across both fuse test points.
Using the scan tool, view start request and starter relay command data during a start attempt if supported.
Measure the relay coil control and relay output with the relay installed, using a fused breakout lead or backprobing.
Substitute an identical known-good relay if the relay is suspect.
tests.expected: The relay is commanded during the start attempt and its output supplies voltage to the solenoid control circuit.

outcomes.label: Relay commanded and switching normally
outcomes.interpretation: The control side up to the relay works; check the wire to the solenoid and the starter.

outcomes.label: Relay is not commanded
outcomes.interpretation: The start request is being blocked or not received; check interlocks, security status, and the ignition switch or start button input.

outcomes.label: Relay commanded but no output, or open fuse
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the failed relay or find the cause of the open fuse before replacing it.

tests.title: Measure control voltage at the starter solenoid terminal during a start attempt
tests.purpose: Split the fault between the starter itself and its control circuit.
procedure: Raise and support the vehicle on a lift or jack stands if needed to reach the starter.
Backprobe the solenoid control terminal with the connector attached; ground the meter to the starter housing.
Have an assistant make a start attempt while you read the voltage, keeping clear of moving parts.
Compare the reading to battery voltage measured at the same moment.
tests.expected: Control voltage at the solenoid is close to battery voltage during the start attempt, per OEM specification.
tests.specNote: OEM minimum solenoid control voltage.

outcomes.label: Good control voltage at the solenoid
outcomes.interpretation: With good power, ground, and control voltage but no crank, the starter or engine rotation is at fault.

outcomes.label: No control voltage at the solenoid
outcomes.interpretation: Trace the control circuit back through the relay, interlocks, and start request.

outcomes.label: Control voltage present but low
outcomes.interpretation: Voltage drop test the control circuit to find the high-resistance point.

tests.title: Check that the engine rotates by hand
tests.purpose: Rule out a seized or hydrolocked engine before condemning the starter.
procedure: Disconnect the battery negative cable so the engine cannot be cranked.
If liquid in a cylinder is suspected, remove the spark plugs before attempting rotation.
Using a breaker bar on the crankshaft bolt, attempt to rotate the engine slowly in its normal direction of rotation only.
Stop immediately if firm resistance is felt; do not force rotation.
tests.expected: The engine rotates through at least two full revolutions with normal compression resistance.

outcomes.label: Engine rotates normally
outcomes.interpretation: The engine is not seized; the starter or its circuit is the focus.

outcomes.label: Engine will not rotate or locks up
outcomes.interpretation: Investigate internal engine damage or hydrolock; do not attempt further cranking.

tests.title: Remove and bench test the starter; inspect the ring gear
tests.purpose: Confirm a starter failure after all circuit checks pass.
procedure: Disconnect the battery negative cable, then raise and support the vehicle as needed.
Remove the starter per OEM procedure and inspect the pinion and the flywheel or flexplate ring gear teeth.
Perform a no-load bench test per the starter manufacturer's procedure, securing the starter in a vise and using properly sized, fused leads.
Compare engagement and free-running current to the published starter specification.
tests.expected: The pinion engages crisply and free-running current is within the starter manufacturer's specification.
tests.specNote: Starter no-load current specification from the starter manufacturer or OEM.

outcomes.label: Starter passes and ring gear is intact
outcomes.interpretation: The starter is likely good; recheck control voltage and cable voltage drop. An intermittent dead spot can pass a bench test.

outcomes.label: Starter fails the bench test, or pinion or ring gear damaged
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the starter, and the ring gear if damaged, then verify cranking voltage drop.

verification: Confirm the battery is fully charged and passes a load or conductance test.
Perform repeated start cycles cold and after a heat soak.
Repeat the cranking voltage drop test and confirm both sides are within OEM specification.
Clear DTCs and confirm none return in any module.

playbooks.title: Battery drains or goes dead while parked
playbooks.summary: Before hunting for circuits, rule out a battery that cannot hold a charge and a battery that is simply undercharged by usage or a charging fault. Measure key-off draw only after the battery is fully charged and every module has gone to sleep, without breaking the circuit while connecting the meter. Isolate the circuit carrying the current with the fuse voltage-drop method so pulling fuses does not wake modules and hide the fault.
clarifyingQuestions: How long can the vehicle sit before the battery is too weak to start it?
Are any aftermarket accessories installed (remote start, alarm, audio amplifier, dash camera, tracker)?
How is the vehicle used: short trips, long storage, or accessories used with the engine off?
How old is the battery, and has it been replaced recently?
Any recent repairs, water leaks, collision damage, or module programming?

causes.title: Weak or failed battery
causes.description: A battery with sulfated plates, a shorted cell, or high self-discharge cannot hold a charge, which looks like a drain even when key-off draw is normal.

modifiers.reason: Battery age or physical condition reported
Cold exposes reduced battery capacity

causes.title: Insufficient recharge from usage pattern
causes.description: Short trips, long storage, or running accessories with the engine off remove more charge than the charging system can replace, with no fault in any circuit.

modifiers.reason: Usage pattern limits recharge

causes.title: Module not entering sleep mode
causes.description: A control module that stays awake, or keeps waking the network, holds several modules and the data bus active and draws far more current than a sleeping vehicle.

modifiers.reason: Intermittent drain or recent programming suggests a sleep problem
Network communication codes present

causes.title: Lamp or switch keeping a load on
causes.description: A trunk, glove box, underhood, or vanity lamp that stays on, or a door, hood, or liftgate ajar switch that reports open, keeps a load or the body module active.

modifiers.reason: Lamp or ajar indication reported

causes.title: Aftermarket accessory draw
causes.description: Remote starters, alarms, amplifiers, dash cameras, and trackers can draw continuously or keep the network awake, especially when wired to constant power.

modifiers.reason: Aftermarket equipment reported

causes.title: Relay stuck closed
causes.description: Welded relay contacts or a relay whose control stays commanded keep a load such as a blower, fan, pump, or ignition feed powered with the key off.

modifiers.match: fan runs|pump runs|blower runs|stays on|hot relay|relay click
modifiers.reason: A load keeps running after shutdown

causes.title: Failed alternator
causes.description: A leaking rectifier diode can drain the battery through the alternator with the key off, and a weak alternator leaves the battery undercharged.

modifiers.reason: Charging system symptom reported
System voltage or generator code present

causes.title: Damaged wiring harness
causes.description: Chafed, water-damaged, or rodent-damaged wiring can leak current to ground or keep a circuit partially powered; a high-current fault is also a fire risk.

modifiers.reason: Signs of wiring damage or water intrusion reported

tests.title: Review usage pattern and battery history
tests.purpose: Identify undercharging from short trips, storage, or engine-off accessory use before measuring anything.
procedure: Ask how often and how far the vehicle is driven and how long it sits between uses.
Ask about accessory use with the engine off (audio, lights, charging devices, idling with high electrical load).
Review battery age, replacement history, and any jump-start or charging records.
If the vehicle has a battery monitoring system, review available battery state data with a scan tool.
tools: Scan tool (battery monitor data where supported)
tests.expected: Usage provides enough driving to recharge the battery between uses.

outcomes.label: Usage should keep the battery charged
outcomes.interpretation: Usage is unlikely to explain the complaint; continue with battery and draw testing.

outcomes.label: Short trips, storage, or engine-off accessory use confirmed
outcomes.interpretation: Undercharging is likely, but still confirm battery condition and key-off draw before advising the customer.

tests.title: Charge and test the battery
tests.purpose: Determine whether the battery itself can hold and deliver a charge.
procedure: Wear eye protection and avoid sparks near the battery; do not charge or test a frozen battery.
Charge the battery fully using a charger mode suited to the battery type (flooded, EFB, or AGM).
Remove surface charge and measure open-circuit voltage.
Perform a conductance or load test per the tester and battery manufacturer instructions using the rated CCA.
tools: Conductance tester or carbon-pile load tester
tests.expected: The battery accepts a full charge and passes the load or conductance test.
tests.specNote: Battery rated CCA and the manufacturer's test criteria.

outcomes.label: Battery charges fully and passes
outcomes.interpretation: The battery is serviceable; look for a drain or undercharging.

outcomes.label: Battery will not take a full charge or fails the test
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the battery, but still measure key-off draw: repeated deep discharge from a drain can ruin a good battery.

outcomes.label: Tester result unclear or battery type not supported
outcomes.interpretation: Use the self-discharge test or a load test suited to the battery type.

tests.title: Check charging voltage and alternator ripple
tests.purpose: Rule out undercharging and a leaking alternator diode.
procedure: Start the engine and measure charging voltage at the battery posts at idle and at an elevated idle with and without electrical loads.
Compare the readings to the OEM charging specification; some vehicles regulate voltage variably, so use scan data for the commanded value.
Measure AC ripple at the alternator output terminal with the meter on AC volts or view it on a scope.
Keep hands, leads, and clothing away from belts and the cooling fan.
tests.expected: Charging voltage is within OEM specification under load and AC ripple is low (general guideline: roughly 0.5 V AC or less — verify against OEM specification).
tests.specNote: OEM charging voltage range or commanded voltage for smart charging systems.

outcomes.label: Charging voltage and ripple normal
outcomes.interpretation: The charging system is not the cause; measure key-off draw.

outcomes.label: Charging voltage below specification
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the charging system (see charging system playbook) before continuing the drain diagnosis.

outcomes.label: Excessive AC ripple
outcomes.interpretation: A rectifier diode is likely failing; confirm with the alternator isolation draw test.

tests.title: Inspect for accessories, lamps left on, and wiring damage
tests.purpose: Find obvious draw sources before connecting an ammeter.
procedure: Look for aftermarket equipment and where it is powered from (remote start, alarm, amplifier, camera, tracker).
With the vehicle closed up in a dark area, check that trunk, glove box, underhood, vanity, and cargo lamps turn off.
Check the instrument cluster or scan data for door, hood, trunk, or liftgate ajar indications.
Inspect the harness for chafing, heat damage, water intrusion, or rodent damage; listen for relays, fans, or pumps running after shutdown.
tests.expected: No aftermarket equipment, all lamps off, no ajar indications, and no wiring damage.

outcomes.label: Nothing abnormal found
outcomes.interpretation: No obvious source; measure the draw after module sleep.

outcomes.label: Aftermarket accessory installed
outcomes.interpretation: Include the accessory in the draw isolation; its presence alone does not prove it is the cause.

outcomes.label: Lamp stays on or an ajar indication is present
outcomes.interpretation: Test the lamp switch or ajar switch and its circuit, then confirm the draw drops to specification.

outcomes.label: Wiring damage or water intrusion found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the damage per OEM wiring repair procedures and confirm the draw afterward.

tests.title: Measure key-off parasitic draw after module sleep
tests.purpose: Determine whether key-off current exceeds specification once the vehicle is asleep.
procedure: Fully charge the battery first. Remove the key or move the fob well away from the vehicle.
Close all doors, or latch the door strikers closed with a tool, and defeat the hood and trunk ajar switches so the vehicle can sleep while you retain access.

Use a low-amp DC clamp on the battery cable, or install an inline ammeter with a bypass or battery disconnect switch so the circuit is never opened during hookup; opening the circuit wakes modules and restarts sleep timers.
Start on the meter's high-current range; never crank the engine or switch on high loads while a meter is in series.
Wait for all modules to sleep per the OEM timeline, recording current with min/max or a graphing meter to see the step-downs.
Compare the settled current to the OEM specification and note any periodic wake-ups.
tools: Low-amp DC current clamp or inline ammeter
tests.expected: Settled key-off draw is within OEM specification after all modules sleep (general guideline: many vehicles settle to roughly 50 mA or less — verify against OEM specification).
tests.specNote: OEM maximum key-off current and module sleep timeline for the vehicle.

outcomes.label: Draw settles within specification
outcomes.interpretation: No excessive draw at the moment; suspect battery condition, charging, usage, or an intermittent draw that needs extended monitoring.

outcomes.label: Draw stays above specification
outcomes.interpretation: A true drain exists; isolate it with fuse voltage-drop measurements without pulling fuses.

outcomes.label: Vehicle sleeps but repeatedly wakes or never reaches sleep current
outcomes.interpretation: Find which module or input is waking the network (ajar input, accessory, or module fault).

outcomes.label: Test setup kept waking the vehicle
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the door, hood, fob, or meter-hookup condition and repeat; probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Isolate the drain circuit by measuring voltage drop across fuses
tests.purpose: Identify which circuit carries the excess current without waking modules.
procedure: With the vehicle asleep and the draw still excessive, set the meter to its millivolt range.
Measure across the test points of each fuse in each fuse box without removing any fuse.
Note any fuse showing a measurable drop and convert to approximate current using a fuse voltage-drop chart for that fuse type and rating.
Use the OEM wiring diagram to identify loads on the circuit, then disconnect loads one at a time while watching the draw.
tools: OEM wiring diagram and fuse legend
tests.expected: The fuse carrying the excess current is identified and the load is traced from the wiring diagram.
tests.specNote: OEM fuse box legends and circuit diagrams.

outcomes.label: Current on a lighting or body circuit
outcomes.interpretation: Check lamps, ajar switches, and switch inputs on that circuit.

outcomes.label: Current on an accessory or power-outlet circuit
outcomes.interpretation: Disconnect accessories and plugged-in devices on that circuit one at a time.

outcomes.label: Current on a control module feed
outcomes.interpretation: Check that module's inputs, software updates, and TSBs before replacing it.

outcomes.label: Current on a relay-switched load
outcomes.interpretation: Check whether the relay is commanded on or its contacts are stuck; substitute a known-good relay.

outcomes.label: No fuse carries the draw
outcomes.interpretation: The draw is on an unfused or main feed: check the alternator, accessories wired directly to the battery, and main cables.

outcomes.label: Draw too small to resolve across the fuses
outcomes.interpretation: Use a more sensitive meter or a low-amp clamp on individual feeds; probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Measure draw with the alternator output isolated
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out current leaking through the alternator.
procedure: Disconnect the battery negative cable before disconnecting the alternator output terminal, and insulate the removed terminal.
Reconnect the battery and repeat the draw measurement after module sleep, or clamp a low-amp probe on the alternator output cable with the key off.
Compare the draw with and without the alternator connected.
Disconnect the battery negative cable again before reconnecting the alternator output terminal.
tools: Low-amp DC current clamp or ammeter
tests.expected: Draw does not change when the alternator is isolated, and no current flows in the alternator output cable with the key off.

outcomes.label: No change with the alternator isolated
outcomes.interpretation: The alternator is not draining the battery.

outcomes.label: Draw drops when the alternator is isolated
outcomes.interpretation: Current is leaking through the alternator or its output cable; inspect the cable, then test or replace the alternator.

tests.title: Check whether the data network goes to sleep
tests.purpose: Identify a module or input that keeps the network awake.
procedure: With the vehicle set up for sleep, connect a scope to the network at the data link connector per the OEM network diagram.
Watch for bus activity to stop within the OEM sleep timeline, and note any periodic wake-ups.
If the bus stays active, review wake-up source data where the OEM scan tool supports it and check the modules and inputs on that network.
Check for TSBs and software updates related to battery drain or module sleep.
tools: Breakout box for the data link connector
tests.expected: Network traffic stops and the network stays asleep within the OEM timeline.
tests.specNote: OEM network topology and module sleep timeline.

outcomes.label: Network goes to sleep and stays asleep
outcomes.interpretation: Network sleep is normal; a module is unlikely to be holding the vehicle awake.

outcomes.label: Network stays awake or wakes repeatedly
outcomes.interpretation: Find the wake source by disconnecting accessories and checking ajar inputs, then check module software and TSBs before replacing a module.

tests.title: Battery self-discharge test off the vehicle
tests.purpose: Detect a battery that loses charge on its own with nothing connected.
procedure: Fully charge the battery and let it rest to remove surface charge.
Disconnect both cables, or remove the battery, and record open-circuit voltage.
Leave it disconnected at room temperature and record open-circuit voltage again over at least 24 hours.
Compare the loss to the battery manufacturer's self-discharge expectations.
tests.expected: Open-circuit voltage stays essentially stable over the test period.
tests.specNote: Battery manufacturer self-discharge guidance.

outcomes.label: Voltage holds
outcomes.interpretation: The battery holds its charge; focus on draw, charging, and usage.

outcomes.label: Voltage drops noticeably with nothing connected
outcomes.interpretation: The battery has high self-discharge and should be replaced.

verification: Recharge and retest the battery after the repair.
Repeat the key-off draw measurement after module sleep and confirm it is within OEM specification.
Confirm charging voltage is within OEM specification.
Let the vehicle sit for at least the customer's usual interval and confirm it starts normally.

playbooks.title: Charging system fault or battery warning light
playbooks.summary: Start with scan data and a battery test, because a failed battery or a smart charging system's commanded voltage can make a good alternator look faulty. Verify belt condition, then measure charging voltage, output current, and voltage drop on the output and ground circuits under load. Replace the alternator only after the battery, belt, wiring, and control circuit have been proven good.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the battery warning light on all the time, intermittently, or only at idle?
Do the headlights or dash lights dim, flicker, or change brightness with engine speed?
Has the battery, alternator, or any battery cable been replaced recently?
Is there any belt squeal, chirp, or whine from the front of the engine?
Are any other warnings displayed, such as low voltage or electrical system messages?

causes.title: Failed alternator
causes.description: A failed voltage regulator, rectifier diode, stator winding, or brush set reduces or destabilizes output, or causes overcharging.

modifiers.reason: Brush and bearing wear increase with mileage
Alternator noise or odor reported
System voltage low or high code present

causes.title: Charging output or ground circuit fault
causes.description: A corroded, loose, or damaged alternator output cable, open fusible link or high-current fuse, or high-resistance connection limits charging current.

modifiers.reason: Signs of cable or fuse damage reported
System voltage low code present

causes.title: Accessory drive belt, tensioner, or pulley fault
causes.description: A worn, glazed, or contaminated belt, weak tensioner, or failed decoupler pulley slips under load and reduces the speed of belt-driven components.

modifiers.reason: Belt noise or wet-weather complaint
Belt and tensioner wear with mileage

causes.title: Weak or failed battery
causes.description: A battery with a shorted or open cell or low capacity can pull system voltage down, overload the alternator, or cause unstable voltage and warnings.

modifiers.reason: Battery age, condition, or jump-start history

causes.title: Loose or corroded battery terminal or cable
causes.description: High resistance at the battery terminals causes unstable system voltage, warning lights, and poor charging even with a good alternator.

modifiers.reason: Terminal condition or intermittent symptoms reported

causes.title: Poor ground connection
causes.description: A high-resistance engine or alternator ground adds drop to the charging return path and can skew regulator sensing.

modifiers.reason: Intermittent electrical symptoms or recent engine work

causes.title: Battery monitor sensor or battery registration fault
causes.description: On smart charging systems a failed battery current/temperature sensor, or a replacement battery that was not registered, causes incorrect charge targets.

modifiers.reason: Recent battery replacement may require registration or reset

causes.title: Generator control, field, or lamp circuit fault
causes.description: An open, short, or corroded connection in the circuits between the engine controller and the alternator (control, field, lamp, or LIN data) prevents proper regulation.

modifiers.reason: Generator control, field, or lamp circuit code present

tests.title: Scan DTCs and review charging system data
tests.purpose: Compare commanded and actual charging behavior and identify circuit or sensor faults.
procedure: Record DTCs and freeze frame data from all modules.
With the engine running, view system voltage, commanded charging voltage or generator duty cycle, and battery sensor data where supported.
Turn on large electrical loads and watch whether actual voltage follows the commanded value.
Note any implausible battery sensor values or messages indicating the battery was not registered.
tests.expected: Actual voltage follows the commanded value within OEM limits, sensor data are plausible, and no charging DTCs are present.
tests.specNote: OEM charging data definitions for the vehicle's charging strategy.

outcomes.label: Data normal, no charging DTCs
outcomes.interpretation: No active control fault; test the battery and measure charging performance directly.

outcomes.label: Generator control, field, or lamp circuit DTC present
outcomes.interpretation: Test the control circuit between the engine controller and the alternator before replacing either.

outcomes.label: Actual voltage below commanded or unstable
outcomes.interpretation: Charging output is not meeting demand; check the belt, then measure output and circuit voltage drop.

outcomes.label: Battery sensor data implausible or battery not registered
outcomes.interpretation: Check the battery monitor sensor connection and perform battery registration per OEM procedure.

tests.title: Charge and test the battery
tests.purpose: Rule out a battery fault before judging the charging system.
procedure: Wear eye protection and avoid sparks near the battery.
Charge the battery fully with a charger mode suited to its type (flooded, EFB, or AGM).
Remove surface charge, measure open-circuit voltage, and perform a conductance or load test using the rated CCA.
Inspect the case for swelling, leaks, or damaged posts.
tools: Conductance tester or carbon-pile load tester
tests.expected: The battery charges fully and passes the load or conductance test per the manufacturer criteria.
tests.specNote: Battery rated CCA and test criteria.

outcomes.label: Battery passes
outcomes.interpretation: The battery is serviceable; test the charging system.

outcomes.label: Battery fails or will not take a charge
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the battery, register it if required, and then confirm charging performance; a charging fault may have damaged it.

tests.title: Inspect the drive belt, tensioner, and alternator pulley
tests.purpose: Find belt slip that reduces alternator speed under load.
procedure: With the engine off and the key removed, inspect the belt for glazing, cracking, missing ribs, and oil or coolant contamination.
Check tensioner operation and indicator position per OEM guidance and inspect pulleys for wobble or noise.
Check the alternator decoupler pulley function per OEM procedure where equipped.
Start the engine and, keeping hands and clothing clear, watch the belt and tensioner for flutter or slip as electrical loads are switched on.
tests.expected: The belt is in good condition, the tensioner holds steady tension, and pulleys run true.
tests.specNote: OEM belt routing and tensioner inspection criteria.

outcomes.label: Belt, tensioner, and pulleys good
outcomes.interpretation: Belt slip is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Belt worn or slipping, weak tensioner, or failed pulley
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the belt drive and recheck charging output before condemning the alternator.

tests.title: Measure charging voltage at idle and elevated RPM with loads
tests.purpose: Determine whether the system is undercharging, overcharging, or regulating correctly.
procedure: Connect the meter directly to the battery posts.
Start the engine and record voltage at idle, then at an elevated idle, with loads off and then with headlights, blower, and defrosters on.
On smart charging systems, use the OEM test mode or command a fixed charging voltage with the scan tool if supported.
Keep clear of the belt and cooling fan.
tests.expected: Voltage stays within the OEM charging range (or tracks the commanded value) under each condition.
tests.specNote: OEM charging voltage range or commanded voltage behavior.

outcomes.label: Voltage within specification
outcomes.interpretation: Regulation is correct at this moment; look at battery, connections, or intermittent faults.

outcomes.label: Voltage below specification
outcomes.interpretation: Measure output current and circuit voltage drop to separate the alternator from its wiring and control.

outcomes.label: Voltage above specification
outcomes.interpretation: Check regulator sensing, grounds, control commands, and battery sensor data; overcharging can damage the battery and electronics.

tests.title: Check alternator AC ripple and output waveform
tests.purpose: Detect failed rectifier diodes or stator windings.
procedure: With the engine running and a moderate electrical load on, measure AC voltage at the alternator output terminal, or view the output on a scope.
Compare the ripple level and waveform pattern to a known-good reference.
Keep leads away from the belt and fan.
tests.expected: Ripple is low with an even waveform (general guideline: roughly 0.5 V AC or less — verify against OEM specification).

outcomes.label: Ripple and waveform normal
outcomes.interpretation: Diodes and stator are likely good; a regulator or brush fault can still exist.

outcomes.label: Excessive ripple or uneven waveform
outcomes.interpretation: A diode or stator fault is likely; confirm with the output current test.

tests.title: Measure alternator output current under load
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the alternator can deliver its rated output.
procedure: Clamp an inductive amp probe around the alternator output cable.
Start the engine, raise speed per the tester or OEM procedure, and apply load with vehicle accessories or a carbon pile where the OEM permits.
On smart charging systems, use the OEM test mode or command full output with the scan tool.
Record maximum output current while holding voltage within the tester's guidance, and compare to the alternator rating.
tests.expected: Output current reaches the rated value within the tolerance in the OEM or alternator manufacturer specification.
tests.specNote: Alternator rated output and test conditions.

outcomes.label: Output meets rating
outcomes.interpretation: The alternator can produce rated current; look at connections, battery, and control strategy.

outcomes.label: Output below rating
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm belt condition and output-circuit voltage drop before replacing the alternator.

tests.title: Voltage drop test of the charging output and ground circuits
tests.purpose: Find high resistance between the alternator and the battery.
procedure: Run the engine with a high electrical load so the alternator delivers substantial current.
Measure from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post.
Measure from the alternator housing to the battery negative post.
If a reading is high, move the probe point by point to isolate the connection, fuse, or cable section at fault.
tests.expected: Voltage drop on each side is within OEM specification (general guideline: a few tenths of a volt or less at high output — verify against OEM specification).
tests.specNote: OEM charging circuit voltage drop limits.

outcomes.label: Both sides within specification
outcomes.interpretation: The charging wiring is good.

outcomes.label: Excessive drop on the output side
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the output cable, fuse, or connection and retest output.

outcomes.label: Excessive drop on the ground side
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or repair the ground path and retest.

tests.title: Check the battery monitor sensor and battery registration
tests.purpose: Confirm the smart charging system has valid battery information.
procedure: Inspect the battery monitor sensor at the negative terminal for damage, corrosion, and correct cable routing per OEM guidance.
Compare sensor voltage, current, and temperature data to meter readings and ambient conditions.
Check whether the installed battery was registered or reset per OEM procedure, and perform it if required.
tools: Scan tool with battery registration function
tests.expected: Sensor data agree with measured values and the battery registration matches the installed battery.
tests.specNote: OEM battery registration and sensor diagnosis procedure.

outcomes.label: Sensor data plausible and battery registered
outcomes.interpretation: The battery monitoring input is valid.

outcomes.label: Sensor data implausible or registration missing
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the sensor connection or replace the sensor, and complete battery registration per OEM procedure.

tests.title: Test the alternator control circuits between the engine controller and alternator
tests.purpose: Separate a control-circuit fault from an alternator that ignores a valid command.
procedure: Identify the control, field, lamp, sense, or LIN circuits from the OEM wiring diagram.
Inspect the alternator connector for corrosion, spread terminals, and damaged wiring.
Backprobe the circuits and check the command signal with a scope or meter while changing the commanded output with the scan tool.
Check each circuit for opens, shorts to ground, and shorts to voltage with the connectors disconnected, per OEM procedure.
tests.expected: The command signal is present and changes as commanded, the circuits test good, and the alternator output responds.
tests.specNote: OEM control signal description and circuit test procedure.

outcomes.label: Circuits good and alternator responds
outcomes.interpretation: The control path works.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or corroded connection in a control circuit
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit and retest before replacing the alternator or engine controller.

outcomes.label: Valid command present but alternator does not respond
outcomes.interpretation: The alternator regulator is likely faulty; confirm power and ground at the alternator first.

verification: Confirm charging voltage is within OEM specification at idle and elevated speed with loads applied.
Confirm alternator output current meets its rating under load.
Perform battery registration or reset if required by the OEM.
Clear DTCs, road test, and confirm the warning light and codes do not return.

playbooks.title: Lost communication and network faults
playbooks.summary: Map which modules communicate and which do not before testing anything, because the pattern points to a single module's power or ground, a bus-level wiring fault, or low system voltage. Verify battery condition and remove aftermarket devices, then use bus resistance and waveform checks to find wiring or termination faults. Replace or program a module only after its power, ground, and network wiring have been proven good.
clarifyingQuestions: Which warning lights or systems are affected, and do they fail at the same time?
Is the problem constant or intermittent (after rain, over bumps, on cold starts)?
Any recent battery work, jump-starting, collision repair, or module replacement?
Are any aftermarket devices installed (remote start, alarm, tracker, plug-in OBD device)?
Does the scan tool communicate with some modules but not others?

causes.title: Network (CAN) wiring fault
causes.description: An open, short to ground or voltage, or CAN-high to CAN-low short in the bus wiring, splices, or star connectors disrupts communication for one or more modules.

modifiers.reason: Bus-level communication code present
Multiple systems affected or recent body/collision repair

causes.title: Module power or ground circuit fault
causes.description: A module that loses battery feed, ignition or wake-up feed, or ground stops communicating and other modules set lost-communication codes against it.

modifiers.reason: Lost communication with a specific module

causes.title: Failed control module
causes.description: A module with an internal fault stops communicating, or its failed transceiver loads or shorts the bus and disrupts other modules.

modifiers.reason: Lost communication with a specific module

causes.title: Corroded or damaged connector
causes.description: Water intrusion, fretting, or spread terminals at module connectors, splice packs, or inline connectors add resistance or intermittent opens on network and power circuits.

modifiers.reason: Water exposure or rain-related complaint
Intermittent or vibration-related complaint

causes.title: Low system voltage
causes.description: Low battery voltage, especially during cranking or after a discharge, makes modules reset or drop off the network and store lost-communication codes.

modifiers.reason: Low-voltage event or battery complaint
System voltage code present

causes.title: Network termination resistor fault
causes.description: An open or missing terminating resistor (often inside a module or harness) causes signal reflections and communication errors on high-speed networks.

modifiers.reason: Bus-level communication code present
A replaced or incorrect module may lack the expected termination

causes.title: Aftermarket device disturbing the network
causes.description: Remote start interfaces, alarms, trackers, and plug-in OBD devices connected to the bus or data link connector can load the network or keep it active.

modifiers.reason: Aftermarket device reported

tests.title: Full network scan and communication map
tests.purpose: Identify which modules respond, which are silent, and whether faults are current or history.
procedure: Connect a scan tool and run a full network scan of all modules.
Record which modules respond and every DTC with its status (current, pending, or history) and occurrence data.
Compare silent modules with the OEM network topology to see whether they share a bus segment, splice, power feed, or ground.
Save the report before clearing anything.
tools: Scan tool with full network scan
tests.expected: All modules respond and no current U-codes are present.
tests.specNote: OEM network topology diagram for the vehicle.

outcomes.label: One module does not respond; others report lost communication with it
outcomes.interpretation: Check that module's power, ground, and wake-up feed, then its network connection.

outcomes.label: Several modules or a whole bus segment silent
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect bus wiring, a module or device loading the bus, termination, or a shared power feed; check bus resistance and waveforms.

outcomes.label: All modules respond; U-codes are history or intermittent
outcomes.interpretation: Look for low-voltage events and intermittent connections; use occurrence data to focus testing.

tests.title: Check battery condition and system voltage
tests.purpose: Rule out low voltage as the cause of module dropouts.
procedure: Test the battery state of charge and perform a conductance or load test.
Record minimum voltage during cranking and running voltage with loads on.
Review freeze frame or occurrence data for low-voltage conditions when the U-codes set.
tests.expected: The battery passes, and cranking and running voltages are within OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Battery and system voltage normal
outcomes.interpretation: Low voltage is unlikely to be the cause.

outcomes.label: Battery weak or voltage low during cranking or running
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the battery or charging problem, clear codes, and retest before any network diagnosis.

tests.title: Disconnect aftermarket and plug-in devices and rescan
tests.purpose: Determine whether an added device is disturbing the network.
procedure: Remove any plug-in device from the data link connector.
Locate aftermarket modules (remote start, alarm, tracker, audio interface) and disconnect them per the installer's or OEM guidance.
Cycle the key, rescan the network, and compare communication to the original scan.
tests.expected: No aftermarket devices are present, or disconnecting them does not change communication.

outcomes.label: No devices found, or no change after disconnecting
outcomes.interpretation: Aftermarket equipment is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Communication restored after disconnecting a device
outcomes.interpretation: Leave the device disconnected and have its installation corrected or removed.

tests.title: Inspect network connectors, splices, and grounds for corrosion and damage
tests.purpose: Find water intrusion, damaged terminals, or chafed wiring on the affected bus.
procedure: Disconnect the battery negative cable per OEM precautions before unplugging module connectors.
Inspect connectors at the silent modules, network splice packs or star connectors, and related grounds for corrosion, water, and pushed-back or spread terminals.
Check known water-entry areas and harness routing points listed in OEM information or TSBs.
Perform a terminal drag test with the correct mating terminal tool.
tests.expected: Connectors are dry and clean, terminals have proper tension, and the harness is undamaged.

outcomes.label: Connectors and harness good
outcomes.interpretation: No visible connection fault; continue with electrical measurements.

outcomes.label: Corrosion, water, or poor terminal tension found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the terminals per OEM procedure, fix the water entry, and retest communication.

outcomes.label: Chafed, pinched, or damaged harness found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the harness using OEM-approved methods (twisted-pair network wiring must keep its twist) and retest.

tests.title: Measure resistance between CAN-high and CAN-low with the battery disconnected
tests.purpose: Check the bus termination and backbone continuity.
procedure: Turn the key off, disconnect the battery negative cable per OEM precautions, and wait for modules to power down.
Identify the CAN-high and CAN-low pins for the bus under test at the data link connector or a network access point per the OEM diagram.
Measure resistance between CAN-high and CAN-low.
Also measure from each line to ground to check for shorts.
Compare the reading with the expected value for the network's termination design.
tests.expected: Resistance matches the network's termination design (general guideline: roughly 60 ohms for a high-speed CAN bus with two 120-ohm terminators — verify per OEM network topology), with no short to ground.
tests.specNote: OEM termination design; some networks (fault-tolerant low-speed CAN, single-wire CAN, LIN, or other topologies) do not follow the two-terminator pattern.

outcomes.label: Resistance matches the termination design
outcomes.interpretation: Termination and backbone are intact; shorts to voltage or branch opens are still possible, so check waveforms.

outcomes.label: Resistance about double the expected value or open
outcomes.interpretation: One terminator is missing or the backbone is open; check the module or harness containing the terminator and the wiring to it.

outcomes.label: Resistance well below expected or near zero
outcomes.interpretation: CAN-high and CAN-low are shorted together or extra termination is present; isolate by disconnecting modules and devices.

tests.title: Scope CAN-high and CAN-low signals
tests.purpose: Detect shorted lines, missing activity, or distorted signals on the bus.
procedure: With the key on, connect a two-channel scope to CAN-high and CAN-low at the data link connector or network access point.
Capture the signals and compare levels and shape to the OEM or known-good pattern.
Note any line stuck at ground or battery voltage, lines shorted together, ringing, slow edges, or noise.
Wiggle the harness at suspect areas while watching the waveform.
tests.expected: Clean, mirrored CAN-high and CAN-low signals at the levels specified for the network.
tests.specNote: OEM network signal levels for the bus under test.

outcomes.label: Waveform normal
outcomes.interpretation: The bus itself is healthy at this point; focus on the silent module's power, ground, and connection.

outcomes.label: A line stuck at ground or voltage, or lines shorted together
outcomes.interpretation: Isolate the short by disconnecting modules and harness sections one at a time.

outcomes.label: Ringing, slow edges, or noise
outcomes.interpretation: Check termination, twisted-pair repairs, and added devices.

tests.title: Test power, wake-up, and ground circuits at the silent module
tests.purpose: Confirm the silent module is properly powered before suspecting the module itself.
procedure: Identify the module's battery feed, ignition or wake-up feed, and ground circuits from the OEM wiring diagram.
Backprobe at the module connector with the connector installed so the circuits are loaded.
Measure each feed with the key in the required position and the voltage drop from each module ground to battery negative.
Use a low-current test light only where the OEM permits, never on network or sensor circuits.
tests.expected: All feeds are present and ground voltage drop is within OEM specification.
tests.specNote: OEM module power and ground circuit identification.

outcomes.label: All feeds and grounds good
outcomes.interpretation: The module is powered; check its network connection, then the module itself.

outcomes.label: Missing feed or excessive ground drop
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the fuse, feed, or ground and retest communication before replacing the module.

tests.title: Isolate a module or device loading the bus
tests.purpose: Find a module or device whose failure disrupts the whole bus.
procedure: Monitor the bus waveform or CAN resistance at the data link connector.
With the key off, disconnect modules and devices on the affected bus one at a time, starting with the most accessible and any aftermarket equipment.
Check after each disconnection whether the bus signal or communication recovers.
Reconnect everything and clear codes afterward; note that disconnecting a terminating module changes bus resistance.
tests.expected: No single module or device is found to disrupt the bus.

outcomes.label: Bus does not recover with any module disconnected
outcomes.interpretation: The fault is likely in the wiring itself; trace the circuits.

outcomes.label: Bus recovers when a specific module or device is disconnected
outcomes.interpretation: Check the branch wiring to that module before condemning it; then check for software updates and replace or program per OEM procedure.

tests.title: Trace network circuits for opens and shorts
tests.purpose: Locate the wiring fault between the data link connector, splices, and modules.
procedure: With the battery disconnected, check continuity of CAN-high and CAN-low from the data link connector or splice to the affected module connector.
Check each line for shorts to ground and, with the battery connected and key on, shorts to voltage.
Flex the harness at pass-throughs and mounting points while monitoring for changes.
Repair using OEM-approved methods and retest the bus.
tests.expected: Continuity is good and there are no shorts on either network line.

outcomes.label: Wiring tests good
outcomes.interpretation: Network wiring is intact.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or high resistance found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit and retest communication.

verification: Rescan all modules and confirm every module responds with no current U-codes.
Clear codes, operate through several key cycles and a road test, then rescan.
If wiring was repaired, recheck bus resistance and waveform.
Confirm all affected systems and warning lamps operate normally.

playbooks.title: Automatic transmission shift quality, slip, or ratio faults
playbooks.summary: Verify fluid level and condition by the OEM procedure first, because low or degraded fluid causes many slip, flare, and delayed-engagement complaints. Use scan data and a road test to tie the complaint to specific shifts, then separate electrical solenoid faults from hydraulic or mechanical problems with circuit tests and a line pressure test. Perform adaptive resets and relearns only after fluid and hardware are confirmed good.
clarifyingQuestions: Which shifts are affected (for example 1-2, 2-3, or engagement into Drive or Reverse), and is it worse cold or hot?
