Does engine RPM flare or rise without acceleration during a shift?
Has the transmission been serviced or repaired, had a software update, or has the battery been disconnected recently?
Any fluid leaks, burnt smell, towing, or heavy loads?
Does the vehicle go into a limp or failsafe mode and recover after a restart?

causes.title: Low or degraded transmission fluid
causes.description: Low, overheated, contaminated, or incorrect fluid reduces hydraulic pressure and friction control, causing slip, flare, harsh shifts, and delayed engagement.

modifiers.reason: Leak or fluid condition complaint
Pickup starvation or heat-related slip pattern

causes.title: Shift or pressure control solenoid fault
causes.description: A solenoid that is electrically failed, sticking, or contaminated applies the wrong clutch or pressure, causing harsh or missed shifts and failsafe operation.

modifiers.reason: Shift solenoid code present
Gear-specific ratio code present

causes.title: Valve body fault
causes.description: Worn valve bores, sticking valves, or a damaged separator plate or gasket disrupt pressure regulation and shift timing.

modifiers.reason: Harsh or inconsistent shift pattern
Solenoid performance or stuck code suggests a hydraulic cause

causes.title: Internal transmission wear or damage
causes.description: Worn clutch packs, bands, seals, or pump components cannot hold torque or pressure, producing slip, flare, and ratio errors.

modifiers.reason: Friction and seal wear increase with mileage
Slip or heavy-duty use reported
Incorrect gear ratio code present

causes.title: Transmission control module failure
causes.description: An internal TCM fault, including failed output drivers, causes incorrect solenoid control or failsafe operation.

modifiers.reason: Communication loss or water exposure reported

causes.title: Damaged wiring harness
causes.description: Damaged transmission wiring, a fluid-wicking or corroded case connector, or a failed internal harness interrupts solenoid or sensor circuits.

modifiers.reason: Solenoid circuit or electrical code present
Connector or recent repair history

causes.title: Transmission adaptive values or software calibration
causes.description: Adaptive shift values that were reset, not learned after a repair, or corrupted, or a calibration addressed by an OEM update, cause harsh or inconsistent shifts with healthy hardware.

modifiers.reason: Recent service that affects adaptive values

causes.title: Transmission speed sensor or circuit fault
causes.description: An erratic or missing input or output speed signal makes the TCM calculate false ratios, mistime shifts, or enter failsafe.

modifiers.reason: Input or output speed sensor code present
Speedometer symptom reported

tests.title: Scan TCM codes and review transmission data
tests.purpose: Identify electrical codes, ratio errors, and implausible sensor signals before any road test or disassembly.
procedure: Record all DTCs with freeze frame data from the TCM and engine controller.
Review commanded gear, calculated ratio, input and output speeds, fluid temperature, solenoid commands, and pressure data where available.
Check for TSBs and software updates related to the complaint.
Save the data before clearing codes.
tests.expected: No current transmission codes and all data plausible for the operating condition.

outcomes.label: Data plausible, no current codes
outcomes.interpretation: No electrical fault is active; verify fluid and road test to characterize the complaint.

outcomes.label: Solenoid circuit (electrical) code present
outcomes.interpretation: Test the solenoid circuit and connector before replacing a solenoid or TCM.

outcomes.label: Commanded and actual ratio disagree or slip is visible in data
outcomes.interpretation: A hydraulic or mechanical cause is likely; check fluid, then line pressure.

outcomes.label: Input or output speed signal erratic or missing
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the speed sensor circuit (see the speed sensor and TCC playbook) before shift-quality repairs.

tests.title: Check transmission fluid level and condition per OEM procedure
tests.purpose: Confirm correct fluid level and look for signs of overheating or internal wear.
procedure: Bring the fluid to the OEM-specified check temperature, using the scan tool fluid temperature reading.
Check the level exactly as the OEM procedure specifies (dipstick, or check plug with the vehicle level and engine running on sealed units).
Use caution: fluid, the exhaust, and the converter housing can be hot, and the engine may be running with the vehicle raised.
Inspect the fluid color, smell, and any debris on the dipstick or from the check plug, and check for leaks.
tests.expected: Fluid is at the correct level at the specified temperature and is not burnt or contaminated.
tests.specNote: OEM fluid check procedure, temperature window, and fluid specification.

outcomes.label: Level correct and fluid in good condition
outcomes.interpretation: Fluid is not the cause; continue with road test and circuit checks.

outcomes.label: Fluid level low
outcomes.interpretation: Find and repair the leak, correct the level with the specified fluid, and re-evaluate before other repairs.

outcomes.label: Fluid burnt, contaminated, or carrying debris
outcomes.interpretation: Overheating or internal wear is likely; inspect the pan and consider line pressure testing before any fluid service.

tests.title: Road test with scan data to characterize the complaint
tests.purpose: Determine which shifts are affected and under what conditions.
procedure: Road test only where it is safe to do so, with an assistant operating the scan tool.
Record commanded gear, ratio, input and output speed, fluid temperature, throttle position, and engine speed.
Test engagement into Drive and Reverse, light- and heavy-throttle upshifts, and coast downshifts, cold and at operating temperature.
Note any slip, flare, harsh engagement, delayed shift, or failsafe operation and the conditions at the time.
tests.expected: All engagements and shifts are smooth and timely with no slip in the data.

outcomes.label: Fault on one specific shift or gear
outcomes.interpretation: Focus on the solenoid, valve, and clutch that control that shift.

outcomes.label: Slip or delay in all ranges, or worse when hot
outcomes.interpretation: A common hydraulic cause is likely: fluid, pump, or line pressure.

outcomes.label: Enters limp or failsafe mode
outcomes.interpretation: An electrical input or output fault is likely; check codes set during the drive and the circuits involved.

outcomes.label: Shifts normal during the road test
outcomes.interpretation: The complaint may be condition-dependent or adaptive; repeat under the customer's conditions.

tests.title: Apply software updates and perform the adaptive reset and relearn
tests.purpose: Determine whether the complaint is caused by adaptive values or calibration rather than hardware.
procedure: Confirm fluid level and condition are correct first; relearning with incorrect fluid level stores wrong values.
Apply any applicable OEM software update or TSB procedure.
Perform the OEM adaptive reset and the specified relearn drive procedure.
Road test again under the conditions that produced the complaint.
tools: Scan tool with transmission special functions
tests.expected: Shift quality is unchanged, indicating adaptation was not the cause, or the complaint is resolved.
tests.specNote: OEM adaptive reset and relearn procedure.

outcomes.label: No improvement after relearn
outcomes.interpretation: Adaptive values are not the cause; continue with hardware tests.

outcomes.label: Shift quality restored after update or relearn
outcomes.interpretation: Adaptation or calibration was likely the cause; verify the fix holds over several drive cycles because worn hardware can improve only temporarily.

tests.title: Test solenoid circuits at the TCM and transmission connectors
tests.purpose: Separate a solenoid fault from wiring and connector faults.
procedure: With the key off, disconnect the TCM and transmission connectors per OEM procedure and inspect for fluid wicking, corrosion, and terminal damage.
Measure solenoid circuit resistance at the transmission case connector and compare to OEM specification.
Measure the same circuits from the TCM connector to check the external harness for opens, high resistance, and shorts to ground or voltage.
Check terminal tension with the correct mating terminal.
tests.expected: Solenoid resistance is within OEM specification at both connectors with no shorts.
tests.specNote: OEM solenoid resistance specification at the stated temperature.

outcomes.label: Resistance in specification at both connectors
outcomes.interpretation: Wiring and solenoid windings are good; a mechanically sticking solenoid or TCM output is still possible.

outcomes.label: Out of specification at the case connector
outcomes.interpretation: The solenoid or internal harness is faulty; confirm per OEM procedure before replacement.

outcomes.label: Fault between the TCM and the case connector
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the external harness or connector and retest.

tests.title: Scope the TCM solenoid command outputs
tests.purpose: Confirm the TCM is driving the solenoids as commanded.
procedure: Verify TCM power and ground circuits under load first.
Backprobe the solenoid control circuits with the connectors installed.
Command the solenoids with the scan tool output tests, or drive the vehicle, while capturing the control signals.
Compare the signals with commanded states and a known-good reference.
tests.expected: Each solenoid control signal matches the commanded state.

outcomes.label: Command signals correct
outcomes.interpretation: The TCM output is working; focus on solenoid response and hydraulics.

outcomes.label: Command missing or incorrect with good TCM power and ground
outcomes.interpretation: Check for software updates and confirm the circuit is not shorted, then replace and program the TCM per OEM procedure.

tests.title: Hydraulic line pressure test
tests.purpose: Determine whether the pump and pressure regulation meet specification in each range.
procedure: Raise and support the vehicle securely, and install a pressure gauge at the OEM line pressure tap where equipped.
Start the engine with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked, keeping clear of rotating parts and hot exhaust.
Record pressure at idle and at the OEM-specified test conditions in each range, comparing to the commanded pressure where available.
Relieve pressure, remove the gauge, reinstall the plug, and correct the fluid level.
tests.expected: Line pressure is within OEM specification in each range and responds to commanded changes.
tests.specNote: OEM line pressure specifications and test conditions.

outcomes.label: Pressure within specification
outcomes.interpretation: Pump and regulation are good; a specific clutch circuit or solenoid is more likely.

outcomes.label: Pressure low in one or more ranges
outcomes.interpretation: Low in all ranges suggests pump, fluid, or regulation; low in one range suggests a leak in that clutch circuit.

outcomes.label: Pressure high or erratic
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect a sticking regulator valve or pressure control solenoid.

tests.title: Remove the pan and inspect debris and filter
tests.purpose: Look for evidence of internal wear or damage.
procedure: Allow the transmission to cool, raise and support the vehicle, and drain the fluid into a clean pan.
Remove the pan per OEM procedure and inspect the magnet, pan, and filter for friction material, metal, and other debris.
Compare the amount and type of debris to normal wear.
Reinstall with new gaskets and filter as required and refill to the OEM level using the specified fluid.
tests.expected: Only a light, normal amount of fine wear material is present.

outcomes.label: Normal wear material only
outcomes.interpretation: Major internal damage is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Excessive friction material, metal, or debris
outcomes.interpretation: Internal wear or damage is likely; overhaul or replacement is usually required, and a fluid service alone will not fix it.

verification: Verify fluid level at the OEM-specified temperature after any repair.
Clear DTCs and perform the OEM adaptive relearn if required.
Road test through all shifts cold and hot, confirming commanded and actual ratios agree with no slip.
Recheck for DTCs and leaks after the road test.

playbooks.title: Transmission speed sensor, fluid temperature sensor, and torque converter clutch faults
playbooks.summary: Use scan data to decide which signal or function is at fault: an input or output speed signal, fluid temperature, the brake switch input, or torque converter clutch slip. Test the sensor and solenoid circuits at the TCM and transmission connectors before replacing parts, and confirm TCC apply and slip on a road test. Low or degraded fluid and a worn converter clutch can set TCC performance codes even when the electrical circuits are healthy.
clarifyingQuestions: Is there a shudder or vibration at steady cruising speed that feels like driving over rumble strips?
Does the speedometer act erratically, or do shifts become harsh or erratic at the same time?
Do the brake lights work correctly?
Does the problem change between a cold and a fully warm transmission?
Any recent transmission service, fluid leaks, or towing?

causes.title: Transmission speed sensor or circuit fault
causes.description: A failed input (turbine) or output speed sensor, or one with metallic debris on its tip or an incorrect air gap, gives an erratic or missing signal.

modifiers.reason: Input or output speed sensor code present
Speedometer or erratic shift symptom

causes.title: Damaged wiring harness
causes.description: Chafed wiring, a fluid-wicking or corroded transmission connector, or a failed internal harness interrupts sensor or solenoid circuits.

modifiers.reason: Circuit low, high, no-signal, or intermittent code present
Intermittent or repair-related complaint

causes.title: Torque converter clutch solenoid fault
causes.description: An electrically failed or sticking TCC solenoid prevents proper converter clutch apply or release.

modifiers.reason: Torque converter clutch code present

causes.title: Worn or failed torque converter clutch
causes.description: Worn or glazed converter clutch friction material, or internal converter damage, causes slip and shudder when the clutch applies.

modifiers.reason: Converter shudder complaint
TCC performance or stuck-off code present
Converter clutch wear increases with mileage

causes.title: Low or degraded transmission fluid
causes.description: Low level or fluid that has lost its friction properties causes converter clutch slip and shudder and can set TCC performance codes.

modifiers.reason: Leak, fluid age, or shudder reported

causes.title: Transmission fluid temperature sensor or circuit fault
causes.description: A skewed or failed fluid temperature signal alters shift and TCC strategy, for example inhibiting converter clutch apply as if the fluid were cold.

modifiers.reason: Fluid temperature sensor code present

causes.title: Brake pedal switch or circuit fault
causes.description: A misadjusted or failed brake switch sends an incorrect brake-applied signal that can prevent or release converter clutch apply.

modifiers.reason: Torque converter/brake switch circuit code present
Brake light complaint

causes.title: Transmission control module failure
causes.description: A TCM with a failed input circuit, reference supply, or output driver misreads sensors or fails to control the TCC solenoid.

modifiers.reason: Communication loss or water exposure reported

causes.title: Valve body fault
causes.description: A sticking TCC regulator or apply valve, or a worn bore, prevents smooth converter clutch apply and release.

modifiers.reason: TCC stuck-off or stuck-on code present
Shudder can result from poor apply control

tests.title: Review speed, fluid temperature, brake switch, and TCC slip data
tests.purpose: Identify which signal or function is implausible.
procedure: Record all DTCs with status and freeze frame data from the TCM and engine controller.
After a cold soak, compare fluid temperature to engine coolant and ambient temperature at key-on, then watch it rise smoothly during warm-up.
Road test while recording input and output speeds, commanded TCC state, TCC slip speed, and brake switch status.
Look for dropouts, spikes, or values that do not match vehicle operation.
tests.expected: All signals are smooth and plausible, and TCC slip drops to near zero when apply is commanded.

outcomes.label: All data plausible
outcomes.interpretation: The fault is intermittent or condition-dependent; review freeze frame and retest under those conditions.

outcomes.label: Input or output speed signal erratic or dropping out
outcomes.interpretation: Test the speed sensor circuit and sensor.

outcomes.label: Fluid temperature implausible or stuck
outcomes.interpretation: Test the fluid temperature sensor and its circuit.

outcomes.label: TCC commanded on but slip stays high or unstable
outcomes.interpretation: Check fluid, then the TCC solenoid circuit, before suspecting the converter.

outcomes.label: Brake switch status does not match pedal position
outcomes.interpretation: Check brake switch adjustment, operation, and circuit.

tests.title: Check transmission fluid level and condition
tests.purpose: Rule out low or degraded fluid as the cause of TCC slip or shudder.
procedure: Bring the fluid to the OEM-specified check temperature using the scan tool reading.
Check the level exactly as the OEM procedure specifies (dipstick or check plug, with the vehicle level).
Use caution around hot fluid, exhaust, and rotating parts if the engine must run during the check.
Inspect fluid color, smell, and debris, and check for leaks.
tests.expected: Fluid is at the correct level and in good condition.
tests.specNote: OEM fluid check procedure and fluid specification.

outcomes.label: Level and condition good
outcomes.interpretation: Fluid is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Fluid level low
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and correct the level, then retest before other repairs.

outcomes.label: Fluid burnt, dark, or contaminated
outcomes.interpretation: Converter clutch wear or overheating is likely; check TSBs for an OEM shudder procedure before further repair.

tests.title: Check brake switch operation, adjustment, and signal
tests.purpose: Confirm the brake input the TCM uses for TCC control is correct.
procedure: Confirm the brake lamps turn on with light pedal pressure and off when released.
Watch brake switch status data while pressing and releasing the pedal slowly.
Check switch adjustment per OEM procedure and inspect the connector.
Verify brake operation before returning the vehicle to service.
tests.expected: Brake lamps and switch status follow pedal position without delay.
tests.specNote: OEM brake switch adjustment procedure.

outcomes.label: Switch operates correctly
outcomes.interpretation: The brake input is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Switch misadjusted, sticking, or signal incorrect
outcomes.interpretation: Adjust or replace the switch and repair the circuit, then confirm brake lamp operation.

tests.title: Road test TCC apply, slip, and shudder
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the converter clutch applies fully and smoothly.
procedure: Drive at steady speeds where TCC apply is normally commanded, with an assistant recording data.
Observe commanded TCC state and slip speed, and apply light throttle to check for shudder during apply.
Use the scan tool TCC output control where supported and safe to do so.
Record fluid temperature and conditions during any shudder or slip.
tests.expected: TCC slip drops to near zero when applied with no shudder, and releases normally.
tests.specNote: OEM TCC slip limits and apply conditions.

outcomes.label: Applies fully with no shudder
outcomes.interpretation: The converter clutch works under current conditions; focus on the signal codes present.

outcomes.label: Shudder during apply or partial apply
outcomes.interpretation: Check fluid condition and OEM shudder TSBs; confirm engine misfire is not the source before condemning the converter.

outcomes.label: TCC does not apply or slip stays high
outcomes.interpretation: Check whether apply is commanded; if not, check the brake and temperature inputs; if commanded, test the solenoid circuit and hydraulics.

tests.title: Test the speed sensor signal and circuit
tests.purpose: Separate a failed sensor from wiring or TCM input faults.
procedure: Identify the sensor type (two-wire magnetic or powered Hall/magnetoresistive) from OEM information.
For powered sensors, check supply and ground at the sensor connector under load; for magnetic sensors, check resistance per OEM specification.
With the drive wheels safely off the ground and the vehicle secured on a lift, or on a road test, scope the signal at the sensor and at the TCM connector.
Check the circuit between the sensor and TCM for opens, shorts, and high resistance.
tests.expected: A clean signal whose frequency tracks shaft speed is present at both the sensor and the TCM.
tests.specNote: OEM sensor type, supply voltage, and resistance specifications.

outcomes.label: Good signal at sensor and TCM
outcomes.interpretation: Sensor and wiring are good; an intermittent fault or TCM input problem is possible.

outcomes.label: Supply and ground good but no or poor signal from the sensor
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the sensor tip and air gap, then replace the sensor if confirmed.

outcomes.label: Supply, ground, or signal wiring fault
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit; if the supply is missing at the TCM itself, check TCM power and ground.

tests.title: Test the fluid temperature sensor and circuit
tests.purpose: Confirm whether the fluid temperature signal is accurate.
procedure: After a cold soak, compare fluid temperature data with ambient and engine coolant temperature.
Measure sensor resistance at the transmission connector and compare with the OEM temperature-resistance chart.
Check the circuit between the transmission connector and TCM for opens, shorts, and high resistance.
Inspect the connector for fluid wicking and corrosion.
tests.expected: The reading is plausible and resistance matches the OEM chart for the measured temperature.
tests.specNote: OEM temperature-resistance chart for the sensor.

outcomes.label: Sensor and circuit good
outcomes.interpretation: The fluid temperature input is accurate.

outcomes.label: Sensor resistance does not match the chart
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the sensor or the assembly that contains it per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or high resistance in the circuit
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the circuit or connector and retest.

tests.title: Test the TCC solenoid circuit
tests.purpose: Separate a TCC solenoid fault from wiring or TCM output faults.
procedure: Disconnect the transmission connector and inspect for fluid wicking and corrosion.
Measure TCC solenoid resistance at the case connector and compare to OEM specification.
Measure the circuit from the TCM connector to check the external harness for opens and shorts.
Reconnect and scope the TCC control signal while the TCC is commanded, if supported.
tests.expected: Solenoid resistance is within specification, the harness is intact, and the control signal follows the command.
tests.specNote: OEM TCC solenoid resistance at the stated temperature.

outcomes.label: Solenoid, harness, and command good
outcomes.interpretation: Electrical control is good; a sticking solenoid, valve, or converter is more likely.

outcomes.label: Solenoid resistance out of specification
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the solenoid or internal harness as confirmed per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Harness fault or missing command
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the harness; if wiring is good and the command is missing, check TCM power, ground, and software.

tests.title: Remove and inspect the speed sensor
tests.purpose: Look for debris, damage, or mounting problems affecting the signal.
procedure: Allow the transmission to cool, then raise and support the vehicle.
Remove the sensor per OEM procedure with a drain pan ready for fluid loss.
Inspect the tip for metallic debris, physical damage, and correct seating, and inspect the O-ring.
Reinstall or replace as indicated and correct the fluid level.
tests.expected: The sensor tip is clean and undamaged and seats correctly.

outcomes.label: Sensor clean and undamaged
outcomes.interpretation: No physical sensor fault found.

outcomes.label: Debris, damage, or incorrect seating found
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or replace the sensor; heavy metallic debris also warrants an internal wear inspection.

verification: Clear DTCs and road test until the monitor enable conditions for the original code have been met.
Confirm speed signals are clean and fluid temperature rises plausibly during warm-up.
Confirm the TCC applies with slip near zero and no shudder.
Recheck for pending DTCs and fluid leaks.

playbooks.title: ABS or traction control warning and wheel speed faults
playbooks.summary: Graph all four wheel speeds on a road test before disassembling anything: a low-speed dropout points to a sensor, tone ring, bearing, or wiring fault at one corner, while a steady offset points to tires. Check battery and ABS module supply, then scope the suspect sensor signal and inspect the tone ring and wheel bearing before replacing a sensor. If the red brake warning light is also on, check the brake hydraulic system before the vehicle is driven.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the ABS or traction light on all the time, or does it come on at a certain speed, over bumps, or in turns?
Does the ABS activate (pedal pulsing, buzzing noise) during normal low-speed stops?
Any recent brake, hub, bearing, axle, suspension, or alignment work?
Were tires recently replaced, or is a different-size spare installed?
Is the red brake warning light also on, or does the brake pedal feel different?

causes.title: Failed wheel speed sensor
causes.description: An internally failed, cracked, or debris-covered sensor produces a weak, erratic, or missing signal at one wheel.

modifiers.reason: Sensors are often damaged during wheel-end work
False low-speed ABS activation suggests a weak signal

causes.title: Damaged wiring harness
causes.description: Wheel speed sensor wiring flexes with suspension and steering travel and can chafe, break internally, or corrode at connectors.

modifiers.reason: Intermittent or motion-related fault pattern

causes.title: Damaged or corroded tone ring or encoder
causes.description: A cracked, corroded, or swollen tone ring, or a damaged magnetic encoder, produces signal dropouts once per revolution.

modifiers.reason: Low-speed false activation or corrosion exposure

causes.title: Worn or damaged wheel bearing
causes.description: Excessive bearing play changes the sensor air gap, and a damaged integral encoder in the bearing can corrupt the speed signal.

modifiers.reason: Bearing noise reported
Bearing wear increases with mileage

causes.title: ABS control module or hydraulic unit fault
causes.description: An internal module, valve, pump motor, or sensor-supply fault in the ABS unit disables ABS and stability functions.

modifiers.reason: Pump or multiple-warning complaint

causes.title: Module power or ground circuit fault
causes.description: A blown pump motor or module fuse, poor ground, or corroded ABS module connector disables the system or causes communication loss.

modifiers.reason: Other modules lost communication with the ABS module

causes.title: Mismatched tire size or pressure
causes.description: Tires of different size, wear, or pressure make one wheel turn at a different speed, which the system interprets as slip.

modifiers.match: new tires?|tire replaced|spare|different tires?|low tire|tire pressure
modifiers.reason: Tire change, spare, or pressure complaint

causes.title: Low system voltage
causes.description: Low battery or charging voltage makes the ABS module disable itself and store supply-voltage codes.

modifiers.reason: Low-voltage event reported
System voltage code present

causes.title: Steering angle sensor fault or calibration
causes.description: An uncalibrated or failed steering angle sensor disables stability and traction control, often after an alignment or steering repair.

modifiers.reason: Alignment, steering work, or stability warning

tests.title: Scan ABS codes and graph all four wheel speeds on a road test
tests.purpose: Identify the affected corner and the type of signal fault.
procedure: Record ABS DTCs with status and freeze frame data, including the speed at which they set.
If the red brake warning light is on or the pedal feels abnormal, check brake fluid level and hydraulic integrity before driving.
Road test in a safe area while graphing all four wheel speeds together, including low-speed stops, turns, and rough pavement.
Review steering angle and yaw data if stability warnings are present.
tools: Scan tool with ABS data graphing
tests.expected: All four wheel speeds track closely, with no dropouts, and no current codes.

outcomes.label: One wheel speed drops out or is erratic
outcomes.interpretation: Focus on that corner: sensor, wiring, tone ring, and bearing.

outcomes.label: One wheel reads a steady percentage different
outcomes.interpretation: Check tire size, pressure, and wear first, then the tone ring tooth count.

outcomes.label: Module internal, pump, valve, or supply voltage codes
outcomes.interpretation: Verify battery voltage and module power and grounds before suspecting the module.

outcomes.label: Steering angle data implausible or not calibrated
outcomes.interpretation: Check steering angle sensor calibration per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Wheel speeds track normally; no current codes
outcomes.interpretation: The fault is intermittent; use freeze frame conditions to reproduce it.

tests.title: Check tire sizes, pressures, and wear
tests.purpose: Rule out tire-related wheel speed differences.
procedure: Compare the size and load/speed markings on all four tires (and the spare, if installed) to the vehicle placard.
Set pressures to the placard specification.
Measure tread depth and note any tire that differs noticeably from the others.
tests.expected: All tires match the placard size and pressure with similar wear.
tests.specNote: Vehicle tire placard and OEM tire matching requirements.

outcomes.label: Tires match and pressures correct
outcomes.interpretation: Tires are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Size, pressure, or wear mismatch found
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the tires, clear codes, and road test.

tests.title: Check battery voltage and ABS module power and grounds
tests.purpose: Rule out supply problems before testing sensors or the module.
procedure: Test battery state of charge and charging voltage.
Check the ABS module and pump motor fuses with a meter across both fuse test points.
Backprobe the module power and ground circuits with the connector installed and measure voltage drop while commanding the pump through a scan tool function test if available.
tests.expected: Battery and charging voltages are normal, fuses are intact, and module power and ground drops are within OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Battery, fuses, power, and grounds good
outcomes.interpretation: Supply is good.

outcomes.label: Low battery or charging voltage
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the battery or charging problem, clear codes, and retest.

outcomes.label: Open fuse or excessive power or ground drop at the module
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the feed or ground; find the cause of any open fuse before replacing it.

tests.title: Check steering angle sensor centering and calibration
tests.purpose: Confirm the stability system has a valid steering angle input.
procedure: With the wheels straight ahead, compare the steering angle reading to the expected centered value.
Turn lock to lock and confirm the reading changes smoothly in both directions.
Perform the OEM calibration procedure if required, then recheck.
tests.expected: The reading is centered with the wheels straight and changes smoothly through the full range.
tests.specNote: OEM steering angle sensor calibration procedure.

outcomes.label: Steering angle data correct
outcomes.interpretation: The steering angle input is valid.

outcomes.label: Not calibrated, off-center, or erratic
outcomes.interpretation: Calibrate per OEM procedure; if it will not calibrate or remains erratic, test the sensor and circuit.

tests.title: Inspect the sensor, harness, and tone ring at the suspect wheel
tests.purpose: Find visible wiring damage, sensor damage, or tone ring problems.
procedure: Raise and support the vehicle on a lift or jack stands.
Inspect the sensor body, harness routing, clips, and connector for chafing, stretching, corrosion, and water.
Inspect the sensor tip and visible tone ring for debris, cracks, corrosion, or missing teeth.
Compare with the same components on the opposite side.
tests.expected: Sensor, harness, connector, and tone ring are intact and clean.

outcomes.label: No visible fault
outcomes.interpretation: Continue with signal testing.

outcomes.label: Harness or connector damage
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the wiring per OEM procedure and retest.

outcomes.label: Sensor damage, debris, or tone ring damage
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or repair as found and confirm the signal before replacing parts.

tests.title: Scope the wheel speed sensor signal while rotating the wheel
tests.purpose: Determine whether the sensor produces a clean, consistent signal.
procedure: With the vehicle safely supported and the wheel free to turn, identify the sensor type (passive two-wire or active) from OEM information.
For active sensors, confirm the supply from the module with the connector installed.
Backprobe the signal at the sensor connector and rotate the wheel by hand at a steady speed, capturing the waveform.
Look for missing or weak pulses, periodic dropouts once per revolution, and amplitude variation; repeat at the module connector.
tests.expected: A clean, consistent signal with even pulses for a full revolution at both connectors.
tests.specNote: OEM sensor type and signal characteristics.

outcomes.label: Clean signal at sensor and module
outcomes.interpretation: The corner is producing a good signal; consider intermittent wiring or the module input.

outcomes.label: Periodic dropouts or varying amplitude
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the tone ring and bearing play before replacing the sensor.

outcomes.label: No signal or no sensor supply
outcomes.interpretation: Check the circuit between the sensor and module; if supply and wiring are good, the sensor has failed.

tests.title: Test the sensor circuit between the wheel and the ABS module
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out an open, short, or intermittent wiring fault.
procedure: Disconnect the sensor and ABS module connectors per OEM procedure.
Check each circuit for continuity, shorts to ground, shorts to voltage, and shorts between the two sensor wires.
Flex the harness through its full suspension and steering travel while monitoring for changes.
Inspect module connector terminals for corrosion and tension.
tests.expected: Continuity is good with no shorts, and readings stay stable while flexing the harness.

outcomes.label: Circuit tests good
outcomes.interpretation: The wiring is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Open, short, or intermittent fault found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the harness per OEM procedure, route it correctly, and retest.

tests.title: Check wheel bearing play and inspect the tone ring or encoder
tests.purpose: Confirm mechanical causes of a poor wheel speed signal.
procedure: With the vehicle safely supported, check the wheel bearing for play and roughness per OEM procedure.
Remove the sensor and inspect the tone ring or encoder through the sensor bore, rotating the wheel slowly.
Where access requires it, remove the brake components or axle per OEM procedure to inspect the ring fully.
Look for cracks, corrosion lifting the ring, missing or damaged teeth, and debris on magnetic encoders.
tests.expected: Bearing play is within OEM specification and the tone ring or encoder is intact and clean.
tests.specNote: OEM wheel bearing play limits.

outcomes.label: Bearing and tone ring good
outcomes.interpretation: The mechanical parts are good; the sensor or wiring is more likely.

outcomes.label: Excessive bearing play or roughness
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the bearing assembly per OEM procedure and recheck the signal.

outcomes.label: Tone ring or encoder damaged or corroded
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the tone ring, axle, hub, or bearing that carries it, as applicable.

tests.title: Run the OEM ABS self-test and function tests
tests.purpose: Confirm an ABS module or hydraulic unit fault after inputs and supply are verified.
procedure: Confirm battery voltage and module supply are good before testing.
Run the OEM self-test and the pump motor and valve function tests with a scan tool, following all on-screen precautions.
Record any codes set during the tests.
After any hydraulic work, bleed the system using the OEM ABS bleed procedure and confirm a firm pedal before driving.
tools: Scan tool with ABS function tests
tests.expected: All self-tests and function tests pass without setting codes.
tests.specNote: OEM ABS function test and bleed procedures.

outcomes.label: Self-test and function tests pass
outcomes.interpretation: The module and hydraulic unit are likely good.

outcomes.label: Self-test or a function test fails
outcomes.interpretation: With supply verified, check for software updates, then repair or replace the ABS unit per OEM procedure.

verification: Clear codes and road test through the conditions that set the fault, graphing all four wheel speeds.
Confirm the ABS, traction, and stability lights go out after the bulb check and stay out.
Confirm normal brake pedal feel and perform a controlled stop in a safe area.
Calibrate the steering angle sensor if it was replaced or the alignment was changed.

playbooks.title: Brake pulsation, noise, pull, or soft pedal
playbooks.summary: Characterize the complaint on a road test first (pulsation, noise, pull, or pedal feel), because each points to a different part of the brake system. Check fluid level, leaks, and pedal hold before disassembly, then measure pads, rotors, and caliper operation against OEM limits rather than replacing parts by appearance. A vehicle with a soft or sinking pedal or a fluid leak must not be driven until the hydraulic fault is corrected.
clarifyingQuestions: Is the vibration felt in the brake pedal, the steering wheel, or the seat, and at what speeds?
What kind of noise is it (squeal, grinding, clicking, or clunking), and does it happen only when braking?
Which way does the vehicle pull, and only when braking or also when cruising?
Does the pedal feel soft or spongy, or does it slowly sink under steady pressure?
When were the brakes last serviced, and were the wheels recently removed or the tires rotated?
Is the red brake warning light on?

causes.title: Rotor runout or thickness variation
causes.description: Lateral runout (often from hub runout, rust on the mounting face, or uneven lug torque) leads to rotor thickness variation that pulses the pedal and steering wheel; out-of-round drums cause a similar pulsation on drum axles.

modifiers.reason: Pulsation or vibration during braking

modifiers.match: tire rotation|tires rotated|new tires|wheels? (removed|installed)|impact gun|lug nut
modifiers.reason: Recent wheel work can introduce runout through uneven lug torque

causes.title: Worn brake pads
causes.description: Pads worn to the wear indicator squeal; pads worn to the backing plate grind and damage the rotor, and very thin pads reduce braking performance.

modifiers.reason: Wear indicator squeal or grinding noise
Pad wear accumulates with mileage

causes.title: Sticking caliper piston or slides
causes.description: A seized piston or corroded slide pins apply uneven force, causing pull, drag, heat, uneven pad wear, and eventually rotor thickness variation.

modifiers.reason: Pull, drag, or heat at one wheel

causes.title: Missing or worn pad hardware, shims, or glazed friction surfaces
causes.description: Missing or worn abutment clips and shims, dry contact points, or glazed pads and rotors let the pads vibrate and squeal or rattle.

modifiers.reason: Squeal, rattle, or click reported

causes.title: Air or degraded fluid in the brake hydraulics
causes.description: Air trapped in the lines or moisture-laden fluid that vaporizes when hot compresses under pedal force, giving a soft or spongy pedal.

modifiers.reason: Soft pedal or recent hydraulic work

causes.title: External brake fluid leak
causes.description: A leak at a caliper, wheel cylinder, line, hose, or the master cylinder lowers fluid level, softens the pedal, and can contaminate the linings.

modifiers.reason: Leak, low fluid, or warning light reported
Soft pedal reported

causes.title: Master cylinder internal bypass
causes.description: Worn internal seals let fluid bypass inside the master cylinder, so the pedal slowly sinks under steady pressure without an external leak.

modifiers.reason: Sinking pedal reported

causes.title: Restricted or internally collapsed brake hose
causes.description: A deteriorated flexible hose can act as a one-way valve, holding pressure at one caliper so the vehicle pulls and the brake drags.

modifiers.reason: Pull or drag at one wheel
Hose deterioration with age

causes.title: Contaminated brake linings
causes.description: Oil, grease, or brake fluid on pads or shoes changes friction on one side, causing pull, grabbing, or noise.

modifiers.reason: Pull, grab, or leak reported

causes.title: Worn control arm bushings
causes.description: Worn bushings let the wheel shift under braking or load, changing alignment and causing pull, clunks, or wander.

modifiers.reason: Pull, clunk, or wander reported

tests.title: Road test to characterize the brake complaint
tests.purpose: Classify the complaint as pulsation, noise, pull, or pedal feel.
procedure: Check fluid level and pedal feel with the vehicle stationary before driving; do not road test with a sinking pedal or low fluid.
In a safe area, make light, moderate, and firm stops from several speeds.
Note where any vibration is felt (pedal, steering wheel, seat), the type of noise, pull direction, and pedal travel and feel.
Repeat with hands lightly on the wheel to judge pull without steering input.
tests.expected: Straight, quiet stops with a firm pedal and no pulsation.

outcomes.label: Pulsation in the pedal or steering wheel
outcomes.interpretation: Measure rotor runout and thickness variation.

outcomes.label: Squeal, grinding, or rattle
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect pad thickness, wear indicators, and hardware.

outcomes.label: Pulls to one side when braking
outcomes.interpretation: Compare caliper operation, lining condition, and wheel temperatures side to side, and check suspension bushings.

outcomes.label: Soft, spongy, low, or sinking pedal
outcomes.interpretation: Stop driving the vehicle; check for leaks and perform the pedal hold test.

outcomes.label: Complaint not reproduced
outcomes.interpretation: Ask the customer for the exact conditions (temperature, speed, after highway driving) and retest; probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Check brake fluid level, condition, and for external leaks
tests.purpose: Find hydraulic leaks and degraded fluid before disassembly.
procedure: Check the reservoir level and note whether it has dropped since the last service (pad wear lowers it slightly).
Test fluid condition with a moisture test strip or boiling point tester per the tester instructions.
Inspect the master cylinder, lines, hoses, calipers, and wheel cylinders for wetness or residue.
Check behind the master cylinder at the booster for fluid seepage.
tools: Brake fluid test strips or boiling point tester
tests.expected: Level is within the marks, the fluid passes the condition test, and there are no leaks.
tests.specNote: OEM brake fluid type and service interval.

outcomes.label: Level and condition good, no leaks
outcomes.interpretation: No external hydraulic leak.

outcomes.label: External leak or low level found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak, replace any fluid-soaked linings, and bleed the system per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Fluid fails the condition test
outcomes.interpretation: Flush the fluid per OEM procedure; degraded fluid can vaporize under heat and cause a soft pedal.

tests.title: Pedal feel and hold test with the engine running
tests.purpose: Separate air in the system from internal or external fluid loss.
procedure: With the vehicle stationary, the parking brake applied, and the engine running, pump the pedal and note height and firmness.
Apply steady moderate pressure and hold for the time given in the OEM procedure, watching whether the pedal sinks.
Repeat with light pressure, which reveals some internal bypass faults more readily.
tests.expected: The pedal is firm and high and does not sink under steady pressure.
tests.specNote: OEM pedal height, travel, and hold test criteria.

outcomes.label: Firm pedal that holds
outcomes.interpretation: The hydraulic system holds pressure.

outcomes.label: Spongy or soft but does not sink
outcomes.interpretation: Air or vaporized fluid is likely; bleed per OEM procedure after confirming no leaks.

outcomes.label: Pedal slowly sinks under steady pressure
outcomes.interpretation: If there is no external leak, the master cylinder is bypassing internally; do not drive the vehicle.

tests.title: Inspect pads, rotors, calipers, and hardware
tests.purpose: Measure wear and identify uneven wear, heat damage, contamination, and hardware problems.
procedure: Raise and support the vehicle and remove the wheels.
Measure inner and outer pad thickness at both ends and compare to the minimum specification.
Inspect rotor surfaces for scoring, heat spots, and lip; check hardware, shims, slide pins, and boots.
Check linings for oil, grease, or fluid contamination.
Do not use compressed air to clean brake dust; use an approved wet-cleaning method.
tests.expected: Pads above minimum with even wear, clean linings, intact hardware, and smooth rotor surfaces.
tests.specNote: OEM minimum pad thickness and rotor discard thickness.

outcomes.label: Pads, rotors, calipers, and hardware in good condition
outcomes.interpretation: No visible wear fault; runout and hydraulic checks are next.

outcomes.label: Pads at or below minimum, or metal-to-metal contact
outcomes.interpretation: Replace pads and measure rotors against discard thickness; also check why wear occurred.

outcomes.label: Uneven or tapered pad wear, heat discoloration, or seized slides
outcomes.interpretation: Check caliper piston and slide operation and perform the drag test.

outcomes.label: Missing or worn hardware, or glazed friction surfaces
outcomes.interpretation: Replace hardware and shims, lubricate contact points with the specified lubricant, and address glazing.

outcomes.label: Linings contaminated with oil, grease, or fluid
outcomes.interpretation: Fix the source of contamination and replace linings on both sides of the axle.

tests.title: Compare wheel drag and temperature side to side
tests.purpose: Identify a dragging caliper or a hose holding pressure.
procedure: After a short drive with light braking, compare rotor temperatures side to side with an infrared thermometer, keeping hands off hot parts.
Raise and support the vehicle and check whether each wheel turns freely after the pedal is released.
If a wheel drags, briefly open its bleeder with a hose into a container: if the drag releases, pressure is being held upstream of the caliper.
Close the bleeder, then bleed that circuit per OEM procedure if air may have entered.
tests.expected: Similar temperatures side to side and all wheels turn freely after release.

outcomes.label: Even temperatures and no drag
outcomes.interpretation: No dragging brake.

outcomes.label: One wheel drags and releases when the bleeder is opened
outcomes.interpretation: Pressure is trapped upstream; replace the restricted hose and check the master cylinder if several wheels drag.

outcomes.label: One wheel drags even with the bleeder open
outcomes.interpretation: The caliper piston or slides are binding; service or replace the caliper.

tests.title: Measure rotor lateral runout and thickness variation
tests.purpose: Confirm the cause of pedal or steering pulsation.
procedure: With the vehicle supported, clean the hub and rotor mounting faces and secure the rotor with lug nuts torqued to OEM specification in sequence (use spacers if the wheel is off).
Mount a dial indicator on a rigid point and measure lateral runout near the outer edge of the friction surface.
Measure rotor thickness with a micrometer at several points around the rotor to find thickness variation.
If runout is excessive, measure hub flange runout with the rotor removed.
tests.expected: Lateral runout and thickness variation are within OEM limits and thickness is above discard.
tests.specNote: OEM maximum lateral runout, maximum thickness variation, and discard thickness.

outcomes.label: Runout and thickness variation within specification
outcomes.interpretation: The rotors are not causing pulsation; check drums, hubs, and suspension.

outcomes.label: Lateral runout exceeds specification
outcomes.interpretation: Check hub runout and mounting-face cleanliness, then correct per OEM guidance (index, machine on-vehicle, or replace).

outcomes.label: Thickness variation exceeds specification
outcomes.interpretation: Machine or replace the rotors and correct the cause (runout, uneven lug torque, or a dragging caliper).

tests.title: Check suspension and steering components for play
tests.purpose: Rule out worn bushings or joints that cause pull under braking.
procedure: Raise and support the vehicle as specified by the OEM for the joint being checked.
Inspect control arm bushings for cracking and movement with a pry bar, and check ball joints and tie rod ends for play.
With the wheels on the ground, have an assistant rock the steering wheel while you watch for movement at each joint and bushing.
Compare findings to OEM wear limits.
tests.expected: No excessive play or bushing movement.
tests.specNote: OEM ball joint and bushing wear criteria.

outcomes.label: No excessive play
outcomes.interpretation: The suspension is not contributing to the pull.

outcomes.label: Worn bushings or joints found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the worn components and check alignment before re-evaluating the brakes.

tests.title: Bleed the brake system and recheck the pedal
tests.purpose: Confirm whether air in the hydraulics is causing a soft pedal.
procedure: Confirm there are no external leaks first.
Bleed the system in the OEM-specified sequence using fresh fluid of the specified type; use the OEM ABS bleed procedure where required.
Watch the bleeder hose for air bubbles at each wheel.
Recheck pedal height and feel with the engine running before any road test.
tests.expected: Little or no air is found and pedal feel is unchanged, or the pedal becomes firm after bleeding.
tests.specNote: OEM bleed sequence and ABS bleed procedure.

outcomes.label: No significant air and no pedal change
outcomes.interpretation: Air was not the cause; recheck for leaks and master cylinder bypass.

outcomes.label: Air found and pedal firm after bleeding
outcomes.interpretation: Air was the cause; find out how it entered (recent repair, low fluid, or a leak) before releasing the vehicle.

verification: Confirm correct fluid level, no leaks, and a firm pedal that does not sink with the engine running.
Confirm pad thickness and rotor runout, thickness variation, and discard thickness are within OEM specification after the repair.
Torque lug nuts to OEM specification in the specified sequence with a torque wrench, and bed new pads per the manufacturer's procedure.
Road test in a safe area with stops from several speeds, confirming no pull, pulsation, or noise.

playbooks.title: SRS / airbag warning light
playbooks.summary: Diagnose SRS warnings from scan data first, because the restraint module identifies the affected circuit and whether the fault is current or history. Any step that disturbs SRS wiring requires the OEM SRS disable procedure, a disconnected battery, and the OEM-specified capacitor drain time. Deployment circuits must never be probed with a test light or ohmmeter, and only OEM-approved load tools or resistor simulators may stand in for a deployment module. Check connectors under the seats, the clockspring by OEM procedure, and low-voltage history before condemning any SRS component.
clarifyingQuestions: Did the light come on after any work (seat removal, steering or column work, interior trim, battery disconnection, or collision repair)?
Has the vehicle been in a collision, or have any airbags or pretensioners deployed?
Is the light on constantly, or does it come and go (for example when adjusting a seat or turning the steering wheel)?
Do the horn and steering wheel controls work normally through full steering travel?
Does the passenger airbag status indicator behave as expected with the seat empty and occupied?
Are there open recalls for the restraint system on this vehicle?

causes.title: Clockspring (steering wheel spiral cable) fault
causes.description: A broken or high-resistance circuit in the clockspring opens the driver airbag deployment loop and often disables the horn or steering wheel switches.

modifiers.reason: Horn or steering wheel control symptoms, or recent steering work
Clockspring wear increases with use

causes.title: SRS wiring or connector fault
causes.description: Loose, corroded, or damaged SRS connectors and wiring, commonly under the seats where the harness flexes with seat travel, cause resistance or open-circuit faults.

modifiers.reason: Seat movement, interior work, water, or intermittent symptoms

causes.title: Passenger occupant classification system fault
causes.description: A failed or uncalibrated occupant classification sensor, or objects and covers on the seat, cause an incorrect passenger airbag status and SRS faults.

modifiers.reason: Passenger airbag status complaint

causes.title: Seat belt buckle switch or pretensioner circuit fault
causes.description: A failed buckle switch or a pretensioner circuit fault (including a deployed pretensioner) sets restraint codes and may affect belt reminders.

modifiers.reason: Seat belt related complaint

causes.title: SRS impact sensor fault
causes.description: A damaged, loose, water-exposed, or failed front or side impact sensor sets communication or sensor faults in the restraint system.

modifiers.reason: Collision or body repair history

causes.title: Restraint control module fault or stored crash data
causes.description: An internal module fault, water damage, or crash data stored after a deployment event keeps the SRS warning on; OEMs typically require module replacement after deployment.

modifiers.reason: Collision, deployment, or water exposure

causes.title: Low system voltage
causes.description: Low battery voltage during cranking or after a discharge makes the restraint module store supply-voltage faults that turn on the warning.

modifiers.reason: Low-voltage event reported
System voltage code present

causes.title: Airbag or inflator module fault
causes.description: An internal fault or damaged connector at the airbag module itself, or an incorrect or aftermarket part, causes a deployment loop fault.

modifiers.reason: Deployment or steering wheel replacement history

tests.title: Read SRS codes, status, and data with a scan tool
tests.purpose: Identify the affected SRS circuit and whether the fault is current or history.
procedure: SRS safety: this test uses scan data only. Do not disconnect, probe, or disturb any SRS component or connector unless the OEM SRS disable procedure has been followed, the battery is disconnected, and the OEM-specified capacitor drain time has elapsed. Never probe deployment (squib) circuits with a test light, ohmmeter, or any powered tool.
Observe the SRS lamp during the bulb check at key-on.
Read SRS codes with status (current or history), occurrence counters, and module status, including any crash data stored indication.
Review occupant classification, buckle switch, and deployment loop status data reported by the restraint module.
Check for open recalls and TSBs for the restraint system.
tests.expected: SRS lamp performs its bulb check and turns off, with no current SRS codes.
tests.specNote: OEM SRS diagnostic procedure for the codes present.

outcomes.label: Only history codes, consistent with a low-voltage event
outcomes.interpretation: Verify battery and charging, clear codes per OEM procedure, and confirm they do not return.

outcomes.label: Current code on a steering wheel deployment loop
outcomes.interpretation: Check the clockspring by OEM procedure, then isolate with an OEM-approved load tool.

outcomes.label: Current code on a seat-mounted circuit (side airbag, pretensioner, buckle, or occupant sensor)
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect under-seat connectors per OEM procedure and check occupant and buckle data.

outcomes.label: Module internal, crash data, or impact sensor code
outcomes.interpretation: Follow the OEM procedure for the impact sensor or restraint module; crash data usually requires module replacement.

tests.title: Check battery and charging voltage
tests.purpose: Rule out low voltage as the cause of SRS codes.
procedure: SRS safety: do not disconnect or probe any SRS connector during this test. If battery disconnection becomes necessary, follow the OEM SRS disable procedure and wait the OEM-specified capacitor drain time before any SRS work, and reconnect per the OEM SRS enable procedure with nobody in the vehicle. Never probe deployment circuits with a test light or ohmmeter.
Measure battery open-circuit voltage and perform a conductance or load test.
Measure charging voltage with the engine running and compare to OEM specification.
Compare with the voltage data or conditions recorded when the SRS codes set.
tests.expected: The battery passes and charging voltage is within OEM specification.

outcomes.label: Battery and charging normal
outcomes.interpretation: Low voltage is unlikely to explain current SRS codes.

outcomes.label: Weak battery or low charging voltage
outcomes.interpretation: Correct the voltage problem, then clear SRS codes per OEM procedure and confirm they do not return.

tests.title: Check clockspring-related functions by OEM procedure
tests.purpose: Look for clockspring faults without disturbing SRS wiring.
procedure: SRS safety: this check is performed from the driver's seat without removing any SRS component. Do not remove the steering wheel airbag or disconnect the clockspring unless the OEM SRS disable procedure has been followed, the battery is disconnected, and the OEM-specified capacitor drain time has elapsed. Never probe deployment circuits with a test light or ohmmeter.
With the key on, operate the horn and steering wheel switches with the wheel centered.
Turn the steering wheel slowly lock to lock and repeat the switch checks at several positions, watching switch data and SRS deployment loop status in the scan tool.
Note any function that drops out or any SRS status that changes with wheel position.
tools: Scan tool with SRS and body data
tests.expected: Horn and steering wheel switches work at all positions and SRS loop status does not change with wheel position.
tests.specNote: OEM clockspring diagnosis and centering procedure.

outcomes.label: All functions normal at every position
outcomes.interpretation: A clockspring fault is less likely, though an SRS-only circuit can still be open.

outcomes.label: Functions drop out or SRS status changes with wheel position
outcomes.interpretation: The clockspring is likely faulty; replace it per OEM procedure, including SRS disable, capacitor drain time, and centering.

tests.title: Check occupant classification status and calibration
tests.purpose: Confirm the passenger occupant classification system reports correctly.
procedure: SRS safety: use scan data only. Do not disconnect seat connectors, remove the seat, or disturb the sensor unless the OEM SRS disable procedure has been followed, the battery is disconnected, and the OEM-specified capacitor drain time has elapsed. Never probe deployment circuits with a test light or ohmmeter.
Remove objects, aftermarket seat covers, and anything wedged under or around the passenger seat.
With the seat empty, compare the occupant status data and the passenger airbag indicator to the expected empty-seat state.
Where the OEM procedure specifies, perform the occupant sensor zero-point or recalibration with the scan tool.
tests.expected: Occupant status matches the seat condition and any required calibration completes successfully.
tests.specNote: OEM occupant classification test and calibration procedure.

outcomes.label: Status correct and calibration passes
outcomes.interpretation: The occupant classification system is working.

outcomes.label: Status incorrect or calibration fails
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the seat connector per OEM SRS procedure, then repair or replace the sensor as the OEM procedure directs.

tests.title: Check seat belt buckle and pretensioner status data
tests.purpose: Confirm buckle switch operation and pretensioner circuit status as reported by the restraint module.
procedure: SRS safety: use scan data only. Do not disconnect or probe buckle or pretensioner connectors unless the OEM SRS disable procedure has been followed, the battery is disconnected, and the OEM-specified capacitor drain time has elapsed. Never probe deployment circuits with a test light or ohmmeter; a deployed pretensioner must be replaced per OEM procedure.
Watch buckle switch status while buckling and unbuckling each monitored seat belt.
Review the pretensioner loop status reported by the restraint module.
Inspect the belt for signs of pretensioner deployment (locked or shortened belt) per OEM guidance.
tests.expected: Buckle status follows each buckle action and pretensioner loops report normal.

outcomes.label: Buckle and pretensioner status normal
outcomes.interpretation: Buckle and pretensioner circuits report normally.

outcomes.label: Buckle status does not follow buckle action
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the buckle connector per OEM SRS procedure, then repair or replace the buckle as directed.

outcomes.label: Pretensioner loop fault reported or deployment evident
outcomes.interpretation: Inspect the connector per OEM SRS procedure; if deployed or confirmed faulty, replace per OEM procedure.

tests.title: Inspect under-seat and seat belt SRS connectors (SRS disabled)
tests.purpose: Find loose, damaged, or corroded SRS connectors and wiring.
procedure: Follow the OEM SRS disable procedure: ignition off, disconnect and isolate the battery negative cable, and wait the OEM-specified capacitor drain time before touching any SRS connector.

Inspect connectors under the seats and at buckles and pretensioners for full engagement, locked connector position assurance clips, corrosion, and harness damage from seat travel. Do not probe any deployment circuit with a test light or ohmmeter.
Correct connector engagement or damage only as the OEM repair procedure permits; SRS wiring repairs must follow OEM-approved methods.
Reconnect per the OEM SRS enable procedure with nobody in the vehicle, then read codes and confirm the SRS lamp bulb check.
tools: OEM service information and SRS repair procedures
tests.expected: All SRS connectors are fully seated with locks engaged, clean, and undamaged.
tests.specNote: OEM SRS disable/enable procedure, capacitor drain time, and approved wiring repair methods.

outcomes.label: Connectors and wiring in good condition
outcomes.interpretation: Connections are good; continue with component checks per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Loose, corroded, or damaged connector or wiring found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair per OEM-approved methods, re-enable the system per OEM procedure, and confirm the code does not return.

tests.title: Check impact sensors and restraint module by OEM procedure
tests.purpose: Confirm an impact sensor or restraint module fault.
procedure: Follow the OEM SRS disable procedure and wait the OEM-specified capacitor drain time before touching any SRS sensor, module, or connector. Never probe deployment circuits with a test light or ohmmeter.
Check impact sensor and module mounting for security, correct orientation, and damage, and inspect connectors for corrosion and engagement.
Reconnect per the OEM SRS enable procedure with nobody in the vehicle and repeat the scan, following the OEM diagnostic steps for the sensor or module code.
Confirm whether the module reports stored crash data, which typically requires replacement per OEM procedure.
tests.expected: Sensors and module are securely mounted, connectors are good, and no sensor, internal, or crash data codes remain.
tests.specNote: OEM SRS disable/enable procedure and sensor/module diagnostic steps.

outcomes.label: Sensors and module check good
outcomes.interpretation: Impact sensors and module are not the cause.

outcomes.label: Impact sensor fault confirmed by OEM procedure
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the connection or replace the sensor per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Module internal fault or crash data stored
outcomes.interpretation: Replace or reconfigure the restraint module per OEM procedure and check all restraint components the OEM requires after a deployment.

tests.title: Isolate a deployment loop fault with an OEM-approved load tool
tests.purpose: Determine whether a deployment loop fault is in the airbag module or in the clockspring and wiring.
procedure: Performed only by technicians trained in the OEM SRS service procedure. Follow the OEM SRS disable procedure: ignition off, disconnect and isolate the battery negative cable, and wait the OEM-specified capacitor drain time.

Remove the airbag module per OEM procedure, keeping your body out of its deployment path; carry it with the trim cover facing away from you and set it face up on a clean bench away from the work area.

Connect the OEM-approved load tool or resistor simulator in place of the airbag module at its connector. Never measure across an airbag or inflator, and never probe deployment circuits with a test light or ohmmeter.

Reconnect per the OEM SRS enable procedure with nobody in the vehicle, read codes, and note whether the fault remains; move the load tool to the next connector point only as the OEM procedure directs.
Disable the system again and wait the capacitor drain time before reinstalling the airbag module.
tools: OEM-approved SRS load tool or resistor simulator
tests.expected: The fault location is identified by whether the code clears with the load tool installed.
tests.specNote: OEM SRS disable/enable procedure, capacitor drain time, and load tool procedure for the vehicle.

outcomes.label: Fault clears with the load tool in place of the airbag module
outcomes.interpretation: The fault is on the airbag module side; inspect its connector, then replace the module per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Fault remains with the load tool installed (airbag module not at fault)
outcomes.interpretation: The airbag module is not the cause; continue toward the clockspring, wiring, and restraint module per OEM procedure.

verification: Reconnect the battery per the OEM SRS enable procedure with nobody in the vehicle.
Clear SRS codes with the scan tool and confirm the SRS lamp performs its bulb check and then stays off.
Confirm no current or pending SRS codes after several key cycles, and that the horn and steering wheel controls work through full steering travel.
Confirm the passenger airbag status indicator is correct for an empty and an occupied seat, and document any open recalls.

playbooks.title: Air conditioning not cooling
playbooks.summary: Confirm the complaint with a performance test and scan data before connecting gauges: whether the compressor engages, what the pressure sensor reports, and whether the blend door and condenser fan work. Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 609 certification and recovery equipment dedicated to the vehicle's refrigerant type (R-134a or R-1234yf), and refrigerant must never be vented. Find and repair leaks rather than repeatedly adding refrigerant, and verify the charge by recovering and weighing it rather than by gauge readings alone.
clarifyingQuestions: Does it blow warm all the time, or only at idle, in traffic, or after driving a while?
Does the compressor clutch click and engage when the A/C is switched on?
Is the air warm from all vents, or only from one side or zone?
Has the system recently been serviced or recharged, including with a DIY recharge can?
Any noise from the compressor, or oily residue at A/C fittings or the condenser?

causes.title: Low refrigerant charge (leak)
causes.description: A leak lowers the charge, reducing cooling capacity and eventually triggering low-pressure protection that stops the compressor.

modifiers.reason: Refrigerant charge loss code present
Gradual loss of cooling or signs of a leak
Rapid clutch cycling suggests low charge

causes.title: Failed A/C compressor or displacement control
causes.description: Internal wear, a failed displacement control valve on variable compressors, or internal damage keeps the compressor from building pressure.

modifiers.reason: Compressor noise reported
Compressor wear increases with age

causes.title: A/C compressor clutch or clutch circuit fault
causes.description: An open clutch coil, excessive air gap, failed relay or fuse, or wiring fault keeps the compressor clutch from engaging.

modifiers.reason: A/C clutch relay control circuit code present
Clutch not engaging reported

causes.title: Blend door or actuator fault
causes.description: A failed actuator, stripped gear, or binding door leaves the temperature door partly or fully on heat, so cold evaporator air is reheated.

modifiers.match: one side|driver side|passenger side|click(ing)? (in|behind) (the )?dash|temperature (won'?t|doesn'?t) change|stuck on heat
modifiers.reason: Zone difference, dash clicking, or no temperature change

causes.title: Cooling fan not operating correctly
causes.description: Without fan airflow across the condenser at low vehicle speed, head pressure rises and cooling fades at idle and in traffic.

modifiers.reason: Cooling fades at low vehicle speed
Cooling fan control code present

causes.title: Condenser airflow blocked or condenser damaged
causes.description: Debris, bent fins, or collision damage reduce heat rejection at the condenser, raising pressures and reducing cooling.

modifiers.reason: Low-speed cooling loss or front-end debris or damage

causes.title: Restricted expansion valve or orifice tube
causes.description: A stuck expansion valve or a clogged orifice tube or screen restricts refrigerant flow, starving the evaporator.

modifiers.reason: Frosting or intermittent cooling suggests a restriction or moisture

causes.title: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor or circuit fault
causes.description: A skewed or failed refrigerant pressure signal makes the control module inhibit the compressor or cooling fan incorrectly.

modifiers.reason: Refrigerant pressure sensor code present

causes.title: Overcharge, air, or contaminated refrigerant
causes.description: Too much refrigerant, non-condensable gases, sealer, or the wrong refrigerant raise pressures and reduce cooling, and can damage service equipment.

modifiers.reason: Recent recharge or service

tests.title: A/C operation and performance check
tests.purpose: Confirm the complaint and see whether the compressor engages and how the vent temperature responds.
procedure: Keep hands, tools, and clothing clear of belts and fans; cooling fans can start at any time.
Set the controls per the OEM performance test (maximum cooling, recirculation, blower speed, doors and windows as specified) and run the engine at the specified speed.
Watch whether the compressor clutch engages or the compressor is commanded on.
Measure center vent temperature and compare it to the OEM performance chart for the ambient temperature and humidity.
Compare vent temperatures from each side or zone and check that temperature responds to the control.
tests.expected: The compressor engages and vent temperature is within the OEM performance chart for the conditions.
tests.specNote: OEM A/C performance test conditions and chart.

outcomes.label: Compressor does not engage or is not commanded
outcomes.interpretation: Check scan data for the reason (low pressure, sensor fault, or clutch circuit) before adding refrigerant.

outcomes.label: Compressor runs but vent air is not cold enough
outcomes.interpretation: Check condenser airflow and fan, then measure system pressures.

outcomes.label: One side or zone warm, or temperature does not respond
outcomes.interpretation: Check the blend door and actuators before any refrigerant work (note that a low charge can also make dual-zone systems uneven).

outcomes.label: Vent temperature within the performance chart
outcomes.interpretation: The complaint may be condition-dependent; retest at idle, in heat soak, or after extended driving.

tests.title: Review HVAC and engine codes and A/C data
tests.purpose: Find out why the compressor, fan, or doors are not doing what is expected.
procedure: Record HVAC and engine controller codes with freeze frame data.
With the A/C requested, view A/C request, compressor or clutch command, refrigerant pressure, evaporator temperature, cooling fan command, and blend door commanded versus actual position.
Note any inhibit reasons the control module reports (for example high coolant temperature or pressure limits).
Compare the reported refrigerant pressure with ambient conditions and, later, with gauge readings.
tools: Scan tool with HVAC and engine data
tests.expected: A/C is commanded on, pressure data are plausible, and doors and fan follow their commands.

outcomes.label: Commands and data plausible, no related codes
outcomes.interpretation: Controls are working; focus on the refrigerant system itself.

outcomes.label: Low refrigerant pressure reported or low-pressure inhibit active
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm with gauges before assuming a low charge; a skewed sensor can mimic it.

outcomes.label: Pressure sensor reading implausible or sensor code present
outcomes.interpretation: Test the sensor circuit and compare its reading with a gauge.

outcomes.label: Compressor clutch relay or control circuit code present
outcomes.interpretation: Test the clutch relay, fuse, and circuit.

outcomes.label: Blend door does not reach commanded position or actuator code present
outcomes.interpretation: Check the blend door actuator and perform the OEM actuator calibration.

outcomes.label: Cooling fan not commanded as expected or fan code present
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the cooling fan control and circuit.

tests.title: Check condenser fan operation and condenser airflow
tests.purpose: Confirm heat can be rejected at the condenser at low vehicle speed.
procedure: Keep hands, tools, and clothing clear of the fan area; electric fans can start without warning.
With the engine running and A/C on, confirm the fan runs when commanded, using scan tool output control if needed.
With the engine off and the key removed, inspect the condenser face for debris, bent fins, and damage, and check that air seals and shrouds are in place.
tests.expected: The fan runs when commanded and the condenser is clean and undamaged.

outcomes.label: Fan runs and condenser is clear
outcomes.interpretation: Condenser airflow is adequate.

outcomes.label: Fan does not run when commanded
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the fan motor, relay or control module, and circuit.

outcomes.label: Condenser blocked, damaged, or missing air seals
outcomes.interpretation: Clean or repair the condenser and seals, then retest performance.

tests.title: Command the blend door through its range
tests.purpose: Confirm the temperature door moves fully and reaches commanded positions.
procedure: Command the temperature door from full cold to full hot and back with the controls or the scan tool.
Listen for clicking or ratcheting behind the dash and watch commanded versus actual position data.
Measure vent temperature change as the door moves.
Perform the OEM actuator calibration if the positions do not match.
tests.expected: The door moves smoothly through its full range, positions match commands, and vent temperature responds.
tests.specNote: OEM actuator calibration procedure.

outcomes.label: Door operates correctly
outcomes.interpretation: The blend door is not the cause.

outcomes.label: Door binds, clicks, or does not reach position
outcomes.interpretation: Test the actuator circuit and inspect for a stripped gear or binding door before replacing parts.

tests.title: Test compressor clutch command, voltage, and ground
tests.purpose: Find out why the compressor clutch does not engage.
procedure: Keep clear of the belt and fan while the engine runs.
Check the clutch fuse and whether the control module is commanding the clutch relay; note any inhibit reason in scan data.
Backprobe the clutch connector and measure supply voltage and ground voltage drop while the clutch is commanded on.
With the engine off, check the clutch air gap per OEM procedure. On clutchless variable-displacement compressors, check the control valve command per OEM instead.
tests.expected: The clutch is commanded, receives full voltage with a good ground, and engages.
tests.specNote: OEM clutch air gap and circuit specifications.

outcomes.label: Clutch not commanded (inhibited by the control module)
outcomes.interpretation: Find the inhibit reason, usually refrigerant pressure; verify pressure with gauges.

outcomes.label: Commanded but no voltage at the clutch
outcomes.interpretation: Check the relay, fuse, and wiring to the clutch.

outcomes.label: Full voltage and ground but the clutch does not engage
outcomes.interpretation: Check the coil and air gap; a seized compressor can also prevent rotation.

outcomes.label: Clutch engages normally when commanded
outcomes.interpretation: The clutch circuit works; evaluate system pressures.

tests.title: Measure high- and low-side pressures with a manifold gauge set
tests.purpose: Classify the refrigerant system fault from pressure patterns.
procedure: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 609 certification. Use gauges and hoses dedicated to the vehicle's refrigerant type (R-134a or R-1234yf) and never vent refrigerant.
Wear safety glasses and gloves: liquid refrigerant causes frostbite, and R-1234yf is mildly flammable. Identify the refrigerant with an identifier before connecting shared service equipment.
With the engine off, record static pressures; then run the engine at the OEM test speed with the A/C at maximum and record high- and low-side pressures.
Compare readings with the OEM pressure chart for the ambient temperature, and note line temperatures, frost, or sight glass condition where equipped.
Keep hands and hoses away from belts, fans, and hot engine and exhaust parts.
