tools: Manifold gauge set for the refrigerant type
tests.expected: High- and low-side pressures fall within the OEM chart for the ambient conditions.
tests.specNote: OEM A/C pressure chart and test conditions.

outcomes.label: Pressures within the OEM chart
outcomes.interpretation: The refrigerant system is working; recheck airflow, blend doors, and controls.

outcomes.label: Both sides low
outcomes.interpretation: Undercharge is likely; leak test before recharging.

outcomes.label: Low side very low with frost at a restriction
outcomes.interpretation: A restriction is likely at the expansion valve, orifice tube, or receiver-drier; recover and inspect.

outcomes.label: Both sides high
outcomes.interpretation: Check condenser airflow and fan first, then overcharge or non-condensables by recovering and weighing.

outcomes.label: Low side high and high side low while running
outcomes.interpretation: The compressor is not pumping; confirm clutch engagement or displacement control before condemning the compressor.

tests.title: Locate refrigerant leaks
tests.purpose: Find the leak before any recharge.
procedure: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 609 certification; never vent refrigerant.
With the system holding enough pressure, check all fittings, hoses, the compressor, condenser, and evaporator drain with an electronic leak detector suited to the refrigerant type.
Use UV dye only if it is already in the system or approved by the OEM, and inspect with a UV lamp and yellow glasses.
If the system is empty, recover any remaining refrigerant with certified equipment and perform a pressure or vacuum decay test per OEM procedure.
tools: Electronic leak detector for the refrigerant type
tests.expected: No leaks are found.
tests.specNote: OEM leak test procedure and approved dye.

outcomes.label: No leak found
outcomes.interpretation: A low charge is less likely, or the leak is very slow or intermittent.

outcomes.label: Leak found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak, then evacuate and recharge by weight to OEM specification.

tests.title: Recover and weigh the refrigerant charge
tests.purpose: Determine whether the charge is correct, low, or over, and check refrigerant purity.
procedure: Performed only by an EPA Section 609 certified technician using recovery equipment dedicated to the refrigerant type; never vent refrigerant.
Identify the refrigerant with an identifier; do not recover contaminated refrigerant into a clean-refrigerant machine.
Recover the refrigerant, record the recovered weight, and compare with the OEM charge on the underhood label.
Evacuate and confirm the system holds vacuum per OEM procedure, then recharge by weight to the OEM specification with the correct oil and retest performance.
tools: Certified recovery/recycle/recharge machine for the refrigerant type
tests.expected: Recovered weight is close to the OEM charge and the refrigerant is pure.
tests.specNote: OEM refrigerant type, charge weight, and oil specification.

outcomes.label: Charge correct and refrigerant pure
outcomes.interpretation: Charge is not the cause; focus on components and airflow.

outcomes.label: Recovered weight well below specification
outcomes.interpretation: Find and repair the leak before recharging.

outcomes.label: Overcharged, or air or foreign refrigerant detected
outcomes.interpretation: Handle contaminated refrigerant per EPA rules, evacuate, and recharge by weight.

verification: Repeat the OEM performance test and confirm vent temperature is within the chart for the ambient conditions.
Confirm high- and low-side pressures are within the OEM chart (EPA Section 609 certified technician).
Confirm no leaks with an electronic leak detector after the repair and that the charge was added by weight.
Confirm cooling fan and blend door operation and that no related codes are stored.

playbooks.title: Engine overheating
playbooks.summary: Confirm a genuine overheat with an independent temperature measurement before testing components, and never open a hot, pressurized cooling system. Check coolant level and leaks with the engine cool, then verify fan operation, thermostat opening, and radiator flow as the engine warms, and pressure test the system and cap. Test for combustion gases before condemning the head gasket, and bleed air per OEM procedure after any cooling system work.
clarifyingQuestions: When does it overheat: at idle or in traffic, at highway speed, under load or towing, or all the time?
Has coolant been added, and how much and how often?
Any recent cooling system work (thermostat, water pump, radiator, hoses, or a flush)?
Does the heater blow hot, or does it turn cold as the temperature rises?
Any white exhaust smoke, sweet smell, or bubbling in the coolant reservoir?
Is there steam or boiling, or does only the gauge read high?

causes.title: External coolant leak
causes.description: Coolant lost through a hose, radiator, heater core, water pump seal, or core plug lowers the level until the system can no longer carry heat away.

modifiers.reason: Coolant loss or leak evidence reported

causes.title: Thermostat stuck closed or opening late
causes.description: A thermostat that does not open, or opens only partly, blocks coolant flow to the radiator, so temperature climbs quickly.

modifiers.reason: Rapid overheat or cool upper hose reported

causes.title: Cooling fan not operating correctly
causes.description: A failed fan motor, relay, control module, circuit, or slipping fan clutch removes airflow at low vehicle speed, so the engine overheats at idle and in traffic.

modifiers.reason: Cooling fan control or circuit code present
Overheats at low vehicle speed

causes.title: Failed water pump
causes.description: An eroded or slipping impeller, failed bearing, or leaking seal reduces coolant circulation.

modifiers.reason: Pump noise or front-of-engine leak reported
Pump wear increases with mileage

causes.title: Radiator restricted internally or externally
causes.description: Scale, sludge, or sealer inside the tubes, or debris and bent fins outside, reduce heat transfer, especially under load and in hot weather.

modifiers.reason: Overheats under sustained load
Internal deposits build with age

causes.title: Head gasket failure (combustion leak into coolant)
causes.description: Combustion gases forced into the cooling system displace coolant, overpressurize the system, and create air pockets that cause overheating and coolant loss.

modifiers.reason: Signs of combustion leakage into the coolant
Misfire codes can accompany coolant entering a cylinder

causes.title: Air trapped in the cooling system
causes.description: An air pocket after service or from a leak blocks circulation at the thermostat or heater core, causing erratic temperature and loss of heat.

modifiers.reason: Recent cooling service, no heat, or gurgling

causes.title: Pressure cap not holding pressure
causes.description: A cap that releases below its rating lowers the coolant boiling point, so coolant boils and is pushed out through the overflow.

modifiers.reason: Boiling or overflow reported

causes.title: Accessory drive belt, tensioner, or pulley fault
causes.description: On belt-driven water pumps and fans, a broken, slipping, or misrouted belt reduces pump and fan speed.

modifiers.reason: Belt noise or charging warning reported

causes.title: Engine coolant temperature sensor or circuit fault
causes.description: A skewed sensor or circuit makes the gauge read hot when the engine is not actually overheating, and can also mis-schedule fan operation.

modifiers.reason: Coolant temperature sensor code present
High gauge reading without other overheating signs

tests.title: Verify the overheat with scan data and an independent temperature measurement
tests.purpose: Confirm a genuine overheat and check whether the fans are being commanded.
procedure: Do not open the radiator or reservoir cap on a hot engine; the system is pressurized and coolant can scald.
Record codes and freeze frame data, then monitor the coolant temperature reading and fan command as the engine warms at idle.
Compare the scan reading with an infrared thermometer reading at the thermostat housing and upper hose.
Stop the test and let the engine cool if temperature approaches the OEM limit.
tests.expected: Scan and measured temperatures agree, stay in the normal range, and fans are commanded at the OEM threshold.
tests.specNote: OEM normal operating temperature and fan activation thresholds.

outcomes.label: Temperature genuinely high, confirmed by measurement
outcomes.interpretation: The engine is overheating; check level, leaks, fans, thermostat, and flow.

outcomes.label: Reading high but measured temperature normal
outcomes.interpretation: Test the coolant temperature sensor and circuit and the gauge input before any cooling repairs.

outcomes.label: Fans not commanded at high temperature, or fan code present
outcomes.interpretation: Diagnose the fan control circuit and module.

outcomes.label: Engine did not reach an overheating condition
outcomes.interpretation: Reproduce under the customer's conditions (load, traffic, A/C on); probabilities are unchanged.

tests.title: Check coolant level and condition and inspect for leaks (engine cool)
tests.purpose: Find low coolant, external leaks, and signs of contamination.
procedure: Allow the engine to cool fully before removing any cap; open it slowly with a shop towel.
Check the coolant level in the radiator and the reservoir and note the coolant type.
Inspect the hoses, radiator, water pump weep hole, heater hoses, core plugs, and the floor under the heater core for leaks or residue.
Check coolant for oil, rust, sludge, sealer, or an exhaust odor.
tests.expected: Coolant at the correct level, the correct type and clean, with no leaks.
tests.specNote: OEM coolant type and level marks.

outcomes.label: Level correct, coolant clean, no leaks
outcomes.interpretation: Coolant loss is not the cause; check fans, thermostat, and flow.

outcomes.label: Low level with an external leak found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak, refill with the specified coolant, and bleed air per OEM procedure.

outcomes.label: Low level with no visible leak
outcomes.interpretation: Pressure test the system and cap and test for combustion gases.

outcomes.label: Oil, sludge, rust, or exhaust odor in the coolant
outcomes.interpretation: Test for combustion gases and check radiator flow; contaminated coolant needs a flush after the root cause is repaired.

tests.title: Inspect the pump drive belt, tensioner, and water pump
tests.purpose: Find belt slip or visible water pump failure.
procedure: With the engine off and the key removed, inspect the belt for wear, glazing, contamination, and correct routing, and check the tensioner.
Check the water pump pulley for bearing play and the weep hole for coolant residue.
Start the engine, keeping clear of belts and fans, and listen for pump bearing noise.
On pumps driven by the timing belt or chain, follow the OEM inspection procedure.
tests.expected: Belt, tensioner, and pump are in good condition with no play, noise, or seepage.

outcomes.label: Belt and pump in good condition
outcomes.interpretation: No visible drive or pump fault; impeller problems can still exist.

outcomes.label: Belt slipping, damaged, or tensioner weak
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the belt drive and retest cooling performance.

outcomes.label: Pump bearing play, noise, or seepage
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the water pump per OEM procedure after confirming flow and pressure tests.

tests.title: Verify cooling fan operation
tests.purpose: Confirm the fans deliver airflow when needed.
procedure: Keep hands, tools, and clothing clear; electric fans can start without warning, even with the key off on some vehicles.
Command the fans with the scan tool or warm the engine to the fan-on temperature, and turn on the A/C if it also commands the fans.
Confirm each fan runs at each commanded speed; on mechanical fans, check fan clutch engagement per OEM procedure.
Check that fan shrouds and air seals are in place.
tests.expected: Fans run at the commanded speeds, or the fan clutch engages at the OEM temperature, with shrouds in place.

outcomes.label: Fans operate correctly
outcomes.interpretation: Fans are not the cause.

outcomes.label: A fan does not run when commanded
outcomes.interpretation: Check fan power, ground, relay or control module, and motor with voltage drop tests.

outcomes.label: Fan runs slowly, only one speed works, or fan clutch slips
outcomes.interpretation: Check for high circuit resistance, a failing motor, or a worn fan clutch.

tests.title: Check thermostat opening and radiator temperature distribution
tests.purpose: Confirm coolant flows through the radiator once the thermostat should open.
procedure: Start a cool engine and monitor coolant temperature with the scan tool while measuring upper hose and thermostat housing temperature with an infrared thermometer.
Note the temperature at which the upper hose heats rapidly and compare it to the thermostat rating per OEM specification.
At operating temperature, scan the radiator face for cold spots and compare inlet and outlet temperatures.
Keep clear of fans and belts, and do not open any cap while hot.
tests.expected: The upper hose heats as the thermostat opens near its rating and the radiator warms evenly with a normal inlet-to-outlet drop.
tests.specNote: OEM thermostat opening temperature.

outcomes.label: Thermostat opens normally and radiator warms evenly
outcomes.interpretation: Flow through the thermostat and radiator is normal.

outcomes.label: Engine hot but upper hose stays cool
outcomes.interpretation: The thermostat is not opening, or circulation or an air pocket is blocking flow; bleed air, then test the thermostat.

outcomes.label: Cold spots or small inlet-to-outlet difference patterns across the radiator
outcomes.interpretation: Internal restriction is likely; flow test or replace the radiator after confirming.

tests.title: Pressure test the cooling system and pressure cap
tests.purpose: Find leaks under pressure and confirm the cap holds its rating.
procedure: Perform with the engine cool; never remove a cap from a hot system.
Install a cooling system pressure tester and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap or given by the OEM, never higher.
Watch for pressure drop over the OEM-specified time and inspect for external leaks, including inside the cabin at the heater core.
Test the cap on the tester with the correct adapter.
Release pressure with the tester's relief valve before removing it.
tools: Cooling system pressure tester and cap adapters
tests.expected: The system holds rated pressure with no leaks and the cap holds and releases at its rating.
tests.specNote: OEM cap rating and pressure test criteria.

outcomes.label: System and cap hold pressure
outcomes.interpretation: No external leak and the cap is good.

outcomes.label: Pressure drops and an external leak is found
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak and retest.

outcomes.label: Pressure drops with no external leak
outcomes.interpretation: Suspect an internal leak; test for combustion gases and check the oil for coolant.

outcomes.label: Cap does not hold its rated pressure
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the cap with the correct rating and retest.

tests.title: Test the coolant for combustion gases
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out a head gasket or other combustion leak into the cooling system.
procedure: Follow the tester instructions; lower the coolant level if required so coolant is not drawn into the tester.
With the engine running and warming, draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid (block tester), or sample with an exhaust gas analyzer where appropriate.
Watch the test fluid color change or analyzer reading, and look for continuous bubbles in the coolant.
Keep clear of fans and belts, and never open a cap on a hot, pressurized system.
tools: Combustion leak (block) tester and test fluid
tests.expected: No combustion gases are detected in the coolant.

outcomes.label: No combustion gases detected
outcomes.interpretation: A combustion leak is unlikely.

outcomes.label: Combustion gases detected
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the cylinder with a cylinder leakage test before engine disassembly.

tests.title: Bleed air from the cooling system per OEM procedure
tests.purpose: Remove trapped air and see whether it resolves the overheating.
procedure: With the engine cool, fill and bleed using the OEM procedure (bleeder valves, vacuum fill tool, or elevated funnel).
Run the engine with the heater on high, watching for air release and temperature behavior, and keep clear of fans and belts.
Note whether air release stops or bubbles continue steadily, which suggests a combustion leak.
Let the system cool and recheck the level.
tools: Vacuum coolant refill tool or spill-free funnel
tests.expected: Little air is released and temperature behavior is unchanged, or air is removed and temperature stabilizes.
tests.specNote: OEM coolant fill and bleed procedure.

outcomes.label: Significant air removed; temperature and heat now normal
outcomes.interpretation: Air was the problem; find how it entered (recent service or a leak) and recheck the level after several cool-downs.

outcomes.label: Little air found, or bubbles continue without stopping
outcomes.interpretation: Trapped air is not the cause; continuous bubbling points to a combustion leak.

verification: With the system cool, confirm coolant level and the OEM-specified coolant type, and bleed air per OEM procedure.
Run to operating temperature and confirm thermostat opening, fan operation, and stable temperature at idle with the A/C on.
Road test under the conditions that caused the overheat (traffic, highway, or load) and confirm normal temperature.
After a full cool-down, recheck coolant level and leaks, and confirm no codes return.

playbooks.title: Coolant loss or coolant leak
playbooks.summary: Determine where the coolant is going before replacing parts: out of the engine, into the cabin, or into the combustion chambers or oil. Inspect with the engine cool, pressure test the system and cap, use OEM-approved dye to trace slow external leaks, and check the oil and coolant for cross-contamination. Confirm an internal leak with a combustion gas test and a cylinder leakage test before any engine disassembly.
clarifyingQuestions: How much coolant is being added, and how often?
Are there drips or puddles under the vehicle, and where (front, middle, under the passenger footwell)?
Is there a sweet smell inside the cabin, windshield fogging, or wet carpet?
Any white exhaust smoke, especially at startup, or any overheating?
Has the engine oil or transmission fluid looked milky or discolored?

causes.title: External coolant leak
causes.description: Coolant escapes from a hose, clamp, radiator, reservoir, heater hose, or core plug, often leaving crusted residue or drips.

modifiers.reason: Visible drips or residue reported
Hoses, clamps, and plastic tanks deteriorate with age

causes.title: Failed water pump
causes.description: A worn shaft seal lets coolant seep from the weep hole, often only when hot or under pressure, and bearing wear accelerates the leak.

modifiers.reason: Front-of-engine leak or pump noise
Seal wear increases with mileage

causes.title: Leaking heater core
causes.description: A leaking heater core releases coolant into the HVAC case, causing a sweet smell in the cabin, windshield film or fogging, and wet carpet.

modifiers.reason: Cabin symptoms of a heater core leak

causes.title: Head gasket failure (combustion leak into coolant)
causes.description: A failed head gasket, or a cracked head or block, lets coolant enter the cylinders or oil, or combustion gas enter the coolant, consuming coolant with no external leak.

modifiers.reason: Signs of internal coolant loss
Misfire codes can accompany coolant entering a cylinder

causes.title: Pressure cap not holding pressure
causes.description: A cap that releases early lets coolant expand out through the overflow and be lost, especially after hot shutdowns.

modifiers.reason: Overflow or boil-over reported

causes.title: Intake manifold gasket leak
causes.description: On engines with coolant passages through the intake manifold, a failed gasket leaks coolant externally, into the intake ports, or into the oil.

modifiers.reason: Leak at the intake or coolant in the oil
Gasket deterioration with age

causes.title: Leaking engine or transmission oil cooler
causes.description: A failed coolant-to-oil or coolant-to-fluid cooler lets coolant and oil or transmission fluid mix, consuming coolant without an external leak.

modifiers.reason: Cross-contamination of coolant and oil or fluid

tests.title: Inspect for external leaks and cabin signs (engine cool)
tests.purpose: Locate visible leaks and signs of a heater core leak.
procedure: Allow the engine to cool fully before removing any cap; open it slowly with a shop towel.
Note the coolant level, and mark the reservoir level to track the loss rate.
Inspect hoses, clamps, radiator tanks and seams, the reservoir, core plugs, heater hoses, and the water pump weep hole for drips, wetness, or crusted residue.
Check the passenger floor, the evaporator drain, and the inside of the windshield for coolant, film, or a sweet smell.
tests.expected: No external leak and no cabin signs of coolant.

outcomes.label: External leak or residue found in the engine bay
outcomes.interpretation: Confirm the exact source under pressure before replacing parts.

outcomes.label: Wet carpet, windshield film, or sweet smell in the cabin
outcomes.interpretation: Check the heater core and its hose connections.

outcomes.label: No visible leak
outcomes.interpretation: Pressure test the system and cap, and check for internal leaks.

tests.title: Check engine oil, transmission fluid, and coolant for cross-contamination
tests.purpose: Detect coolant entering the oil or fluid, or oil entering the coolant.
procedure: With the engine cool, check the dipstick and oil fill cap for milky or foamy residue.
Check transmission fluid appearance where the check procedure allows.
Check the coolant for an oil film or sludge.
Send an oil sample for glycol analysis if results are unclear.
tests.expected: Oil, fluid, and coolant are each free of the other.

outcomes.label: No cross-contamination
outcomes.interpretation: Internal leaks into the oil are less likely, though coolant can still be burned in the cylinders.

outcomes.label: Coolant in the engine oil or transmission fluid
outcomes.interpretation: Do not continue operating the engine; locate the internal leak with pressure and leakage tests.

outcomes.label: Oil or transmission fluid in the coolant
outcomes.interpretation: Test the oil cooler or transmission cooler per OEM procedure.

tests.title: Check for a heater core leak
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out coolant leaking inside the HVAC case.
procedure: Check the carpet under the HVAC case and the evaporator drain outlet for coolant using test strips or smell.
Run the heater on high and check for windshield film or fog and a sweet odor.
Inspect the heater hose connections at the firewall.
Where the OEM procedure allows, pressure test the heater core separately.
tests.expected: No coolant inside the cabin or at the evaporator drain.

outcomes.label: No signs of a heater core leak
outcomes.interpretation: The heater core is not the source.

outcomes.label: Coolant found in the cabin or at the evaporator drain
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the heater core per OEM procedure (SRS precautions apply if dash removal is required).

tests.title: Pressure test the cooling system and cap
tests.purpose: Reveal leaks that appear only under pressure and confirm the cap holds.
procedure: Perform with the engine cool; never remove a cap from a hot system.
Pump the system to the pressure stamped on the cap or given by the OEM, never higher.
Watch for pressure drop over the OEM-specified time and inspect the engine bay and cabin for leaks while pressurized.
Test the cap on the tester with the correct adapter, then release pressure with the tester's relief valve.
tools: Cooling system pressure tester and cap adapters
tests.expected: The system holds rated pressure with no leaks and the cap holds its rating.
tests.specNote: OEM cap rating and pressure test criteria.

outcomes.label: System and cap hold pressure
outcomes.interpretation: No leak under cold pressure; a hot-only leak or an internal leak is still possible.

outcomes.label: Pressure drops and a leak is found (engine bay or cabin)
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the leak found and retest.

outcomes.label: Pressure drops with no visible leak
outcomes.interpretation: An internal leak is likely; check for combustion gases, oil contamination, and cylinder leakage.

outcomes.label: Cap does not hold its rated pressure
outcomes.interpretation: Replace the cap with the correct rating and recheck the loss rate.

tests.title: Trace slow leaks with OEM-approved coolant dye
tests.purpose: Find a slow or hot-only external leak.
procedure: Add an OEM-approved coolant UV dye in the amount the dye manufacturer specifies.
Run the engine to operating temperature or drive the vehicle, keeping clear of fans and belts, then let it cool.
Inspect the engine bay, heater hoses, and cabin floor with a UV lamp and yellow glasses.
Clean the leak area and recheck after repair.
tests.expected: No dye trace is found outside the cooling system.

outcomes.label: No dye trace found
outcomes.interpretation: An external leak is unlikely; focus on internal leaks and the cap.

outcomes.label: Dye trace found at a leak source
outcomes.interpretation: Repair the component at the traced source and recheck.

tests.title: Test the coolant for combustion gases
tests.purpose: Confirm or rule out combustion leaking into the cooling system.
procedure: Follow the tester instructions; lower the coolant level if required so coolant is not drawn into the tester.
With the engine running and warming, draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid, keeping clear of fans and belts.
Watch for a color change in the test fluid and for continuous bubbles in the coolant.
Never open a cap on a hot, pressurized system.
tools: Combustion leak (block) tester and test fluid
tests.expected: No combustion gases are detected.

outcomes.label: No combustion gases detected
outcomes.interpretation: A combustion leak into the coolant is unlikely; coolant entering a cylinder only on the intake side is still possible.

outcomes.label: Combustion gases detected
outcomes.interpretation: Identify the cylinder with a cylinder leakage test before disassembly.

tests.title: Cylinder leakage test and borescope inspection
tests.purpose: Identify which cylinder is involved in an internal coolant leak.
procedure: With the engine cool and the key removed, remove the spark plugs and note any plug that is unusually clean or wet with coolant.
Perform a cylinder leakage test on each cylinder at top dead center, watching the coolant reservoir for bubbles.
Inspect piston tops and cylinder walls with a borescope for steam-cleaned areas or coolant.
Relieve pressure and hold the crankshaft securely while testing, since the engine can rotate under air pressure.
tests.expected: Leakage within OEM or tester guidance with no bubbles in the coolant and no signs of coolant in any cylinder.
tests.specNote: OEM or tester leakage guidance for the engine.

outcomes.label: No coolant path found in any cylinder
outcomes.interpretation: A head gasket leak is unlikely; recheck the intake gasket and coolers.

outcomes.label: Bubbles in the coolant or coolant evidence in a cylinder
outcomes.interpretation: An internal leak is confirmed at that cylinder; check head and block flatness and cracks during repair.

verification: After repair, pressure test the cool system to the cap rating and confirm no pressure drop.
Refill with OEM-specified coolant and bleed air per OEM procedure.
Heat cycle the engine, then recheck the level after a full cool-down and again after several days of driving.
If an internal leak was repaired, confirm clean oil and coolant and no combustion gases in the coolant.
